articleTitle: Analysis of Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter(UART)
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Modern communication systems depend heavily on the Universal Asynchronous Receiver Transmitter (UART), which makes it easier for the devices to transmit data serially. An overview of UART communication, its basic ideas, and its many uses are given in this abstract. The Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter (UART) is a communication protocol use to send information to computer peripheral devices. UART can operate in both half- duplex and full-duplex modes, typically transmitting one byte of data. In serial port transmission, the format is usually 10 or 11 bits, including eight data bits, one stop bit, one optional bit, and one start bit. Asynchronous communication, a key feature of UART, is known for its stable and straightforward design. Additional features like error detection, baud rate options, flow of hardware control have been made possible by improving in UART technology. These changes address the changing needs of modern communication networks and promote accuracy of data and performance. In recent technology, UART transmitters and receivers have become essential hardware components. Researchers are actively working to reduce power consumption and enhance the transmission speed of UART transceivers.

articleTitle: Detection of Brain Stroke Using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The organ known as the brain, which is securely protected within the skull and consists of three main parts, namely the cerebrum, cerebellum, and brainstem, is an incredibly complex and intriguing component of the human body. Stroke, a condition that ranks as the second leading cause of death worldwide, necessitates immediate treatment in order to prevent any potential damage to the brain. The early identification of a brain stroke can prove instrumental in mitigating its severity or even preventing it altogether, thereby reducing the mortality rates associated with this ailment. One promising approach to achieve this is the application of machine learning algorithms that have the ability to detect and analyze risk variables. The present research endeavors to provide a comprehensive model that encompasses a systematic method for accurately predicting the occurrence of brain strokes. In order to ensure the efficiency and reliability of our proposed model, a meticulous and thorough process of data collection, data preprocessing, and data transformation techniques have been meticulously employed. To construct the model, a dataset specifically tailored to brain strokes was utilized, and a standardized technique was applied to normalize the data. During the training and testing phases, various classifiers such as KNN, Naïve Bias, Random Forest were implemented to discern their individual performance levels. Based on the results obtained when utilizing the RF classifier, it can be confidently concluded that our proposed model exhibits the highest degree of accuracy.

articleTitle: A Framework for Big Data Security Using MapReduce in IoT Enabled Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: With the increase in number of IoT devices day by day, a large amount of unstructured, structured and semi-structured data is being generated, collectively termed as big data. The amount of data stored and processed in the cloud is increasing at a rapid pace. The traditional storage devices cannot meet the requirement of the cloud at both hardware and software levels. There is a need for a mechanism which can handle this issue. Hadoop is a platform which can overcome this big data issue. Hadoop uses HDFS and Map Reduce to process large quantity of data in the cloud system. It is also essential to ensure big data security generated by IoT devices and only the authorized users can access the data. Therefore, this research aims to secure big data using RSA. MapReduce is used to process and encrypt big data as it helps in parallel processing of the data in few seconds. This research paper presents a comparative study focused on the encryption time performance in Hadoop, specifically examining the impact of increasing mappers on the overall encryption process.

articleTitle: CMOS Implementation of a Piecewise Linear Activation Function Based Neuron Unit for Neural Network Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this research, the architecture of a piecewise linear (PL) activation function based Neuron Unit for Neural Network Accelerator has been proposed. The Neuron Unit is designed and simulated in CMOS 90 nm process. At first, a 4*4 Array multiplier is designed, followed by a 10-bit register unit to implement a MAC unit. A 10-bit digital Magnitude Comparator circuit is being used to implement the PL activation function. The PL activation function, along with a Neuron Response Register and the MAC unit completes the overall architecture of the proposed Neuron Unit. The design has 100% accuracy with 18.75 pJ energy and 28.85 μW power consumption.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of ZnO/CsSnGeI3/CuSCN Perovskite Solar Cells Using Numerical Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Perovskite materials have been proven to be a competent choice for an efficient solar cell. The most used perovskite materials utilize lead as one of the components which impose restrictions over environmental issues. Hence, we have made a careful search for environmentally friendly perovskite materials. Cesium tin-germanium triiodide (CsSnGeI3) is one of the perovskite materials which has shown better efficiency. This study has used Cesium tin-germanium triiodide (CsSnGeI3) as absorber layer, ZnO as an (ETL) and CuSCN as (HTL). We have used Solar cell capacitance simulator (SCAPS-1D) software for simulation of the proposed solar cell device. To better understand their effects and increase the efficiency of our solar cell, we have changed densities of defect and depth of the perovskite layer, the density of interface defects, and the depth of ETL and HTL. Additionally, we have used different metals as work contact to analyze its effect on our solar cell efficiency. Further, we have investigated the influence of ETL electron affinity variation on the performance of photovoltaic cells. Later, we have also varied the temperature to analyze its influence on solar cell parameters. The preliminary simulation of the solar cell showed the efficiency of 26.06%, open circuit voltage (Voc) of 1.04 V, fill factor (FF) of 88.34% and short-circuit density (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf>) of 28.32 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>•

articleTitle: An Enhanced Deep Learning Approach for Disease Classification from Respiratory Sound
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Technological progress has revolutionized the automated classification of respiratory diseases, harnessing the complex acoustic data inherent in the human respiratory system. This data serves as a crucial resource for identifying various respiratory conditions. Traditional diagnostic methods face challenges like high costs and limited awareness, underscoring the need for practical, non-invasive alternatives. Hence, the analysis of respiratory sounds emerges as a cost-efficient solution for effective disease classification in diverse healthcare settings. This paper introduces an optimized deep-learning model tailored explicitly for respiratory disease classification. By utilizing COPD audio data from Kaggle and extracting features such as MFCC and spectrograms, our neural network model achieves outstanding performance, boasting an accuracy of 0.93. This advancement facilitates early detection and timely intervention and addresses the limitations of traditional diagnostic approaches, paving the way for more accessible and accurate healthcare solutions in respiratory medicine.

articleTitle: Detection of Manipulated Multimedia In Digital Forensics Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The surge in digital media usage has spurred an uptick in multimedia manipulation., spanning images., videos., and audio. This manipulation., with its potential to spread misinformation and manipulate public opinion., poses serious threats. Detecting genuine from fake media is challenging due to the diverse tools employed. Consequently., cybercrime involving manipulated media is on the rise. Researchers are countering this issue with machine learning techniques., particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). This paper presents an application leveraging CNN s to identify genuine and fake media., bolstered by results from experiments on real and manipulated datasets., yielding high accuracy and robustness. Deep learning models excel in detecting various manipulation types., positioning them as potent weapons against manipulated content proliferation. To ascertain the models' effectiveness., the study includes comprehensive validation., testing procedures., and robustness analyses against sophisticated manipulations., including adversarial attacks and deepfake variations. This research advances multimedia forensics., offering a holistic approach to detect manipulated media with deep learning models., underscoring CNN s' effectiveness in curbing manipulated content dissemination., and emphasizing the necessity of ongoing advancements to tackle the evolving multimedia manipulation landscape.

articleTitle: Proposing A Modified Proof of Stake System to Counter 51% Attack in Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Blockchain technology has revolutionized many sectors in the past few years. From its application in health care, digital currencies to building smart cities, many sectors have incorporated blockchain based mechanisms to produce better and efficient solutions to many of their long-lasting problems. The technology itself is fast and the reliance of some sectors on it has improved the overall performance of the applications. One of the most important and sought after applications of blockchain is in digital currencies. Cryptocurrencies are used in many different areas now a days and have become the go to investment destination for many individuals. Although blockchain is secured but it has many underlying security issues which need to be addressed to make this emerging technique more reliable. One of the issues with blockchain is double spending or 51% attack in which the miners authenticate suspicious transactions which result in heavy loss. In this paper, a new consensus mechanism called Modified Proof of Stake to defy 51% attack in blockchain is proposed.

articleTitle: Performance of Tri-Band Hexagonal Split-Ring Resonator Antennas For WLAN, Bluetooth and WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Novel triband closed hexagonal split-ring resonator (CH-SRR) with metallic loading and open hexagonal split-ring resonator (OH-SRR) antennas using CPW-feed are proposed These antennas are simulated on an affordable FR4 substrate with a size of 38x38mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna's return loss, radiation pattern, and surface current propagation are examined. The findings show that the OH-SRR antenna offers a good radiation efficiency of 82.69%, 82.49%, and 73.82% at 2.4 GHz, 3.78 GHz, and 5.775 GHz resonating frequencies, while the CH-SRR antenna offers a broad impedance bandwidth of 12.85% (2.345-2.66 GHz), 41.40% (3.14-4.705 GHz), and 10.56% (5.39-6 GHz) respectively. Both antennas are reportedly compact offering moderate gain between 1 to 3.8 dBi in the frequency band of 2.4-6 GHz. For both antennas, Dumbbell-shaped broader E-plane and narrower H-plane patterns are obtained, and as frequency increases, the radiation patterns become more directional, which results in high gain. Thus, these proposed antennas are suitable candidates for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and WiMAX applications.

articleTitle: FruitfulInsight: IOT and ML-Based System to Predict Expiry of Fruits
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This study discusses a project introducing an in-tegrated food quality checking system, merging the Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning technologies. The primary objective is to combat the common issue of non-preservative food spoilage due to various factors. Leveraging machine learning and IoT, the project aims to provide effective solutions to this problem in the form of a low-cost, portable electronic nose (Smart electronic nose) that can predict the expiry of fruits so that they can be consumed accordingly. The sensors, featuring metal oxide semiconductors - the MQ2 sensor and DHT11 sensor are interfaced with Arduino Uno and Node MCU for creating, storing, and analyzing the dataset containing the levels of gas emissions, humidity, and temperature of fruits with the help of a machine learning algorithms and IoT. After utilizing various regression algorithms such as Linear Regression, Random Forest Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Support Vector Regression (SVR), the Smart electronic nose was finally able to predict the expiry of bananas with a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.1207. This underscores its potential for assessing fruit freshness and predicting expiry dates, contributing significantly in reducing food wastage.

articleTitle: AI Empowered MOOCs Usage and Its Impact on Service Quality in Higher Education Institute in India
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In context to the current world scenario developing an AI empowered learner-centered environments was not only a tendency but a requirement for sustainable teaching and learning in universities. Thus, our study aims to aims to evaluate how AI empowered MOOCs usage by students impact the service quality of higher education institutions. Using the UTAT model and the HEdPERF scale the questionnaire was used to collect responses through an online survey from the students studying in Universities who have completed at least one AI assisted MOOC course. The result of the study reveal that the MOOC usage of students positively impact the service quality of educational institutions. The implication of the study suggest that the students must be explained about the benefits of studying from AI enabled MOOC platform to get better output.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Models for Software Defect Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: With the increasing reliance on automatic software-based applications, it is critical to automate software defect classification and assure software dependability. This article proposes an expert-based automatic software flaw classification system. Defect report categorization is the process of categorizing defects into predefined groups. Many machine learning (ML) algorithms have recently been presented to categorize defect in various classes. This research proposes a classification model based on the Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) network and Convolution Neural Network (CNN) that uses these deep learning (DL) models to categorize defect reports by generating new word embedding from the defect reports. In terms of recall, accuracy and precision, the results are compared to pre-trained word embedding using Google's word2vec. According to the experimental results, LSTM beats the other models utilized in the study. On the redmine dataset, LSTM achieves a maximum accuracy of 70%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Sound Intensity of Moving Source using Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This area of research focuses on creating physical experiments with real media of this kind and examining the significance of various media outlets on motivation and learning. Using the several sensors present in an everyday smartphone, including an accelerometer, light sensor, and magnetic field sensor, we have modified conventional physics laboratory sessions. In this article, our main aim is “Analysis of Sound Intensity of moving source Using a Smartphone” by using sensors in a smartphone. The sound intensity sensor in smartphones has practical uses in everyday physical settings.

articleTitle: FedHNN: A Federated Learning Based Hybrid Neural Network for Real-Time Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks are vulnerable to intrusions. Intrusions are increasing with demand of Wireless networks creating threats of information leaks and disruption. Centralized anomaly based intrusion detection systems creates bottleneck in bandwidth and increase energy utilization of the nodes. In this paper, a distributed learning approach is employed to update the intrusion detection system in real-time. A federated learning based CNN-LSTM is trained on several local client nodes for real-time updates of the system. Distributed training and centralized testing is performed on the NSL-KDD dataset. The proposed gave high accuracy of 97.68% with very low loss of 0.1568. The results outperform state of the art methods with low computational requirements.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Denoiser: An Approach for Salt and Pepper Noise Removal in Digital Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Digital images often suffer from salt and pepper noise, adversely impacting image quality and subsequent processing tasks. This paper introduces an innovative method for salt and pepper noise removal employing fuzzy logic. The proposed approach first intelligently identify noisy pixels by considering both spatial and intensity information. Following the identification process, a fuzzy filtering strategy is applied to dynamically adjust pixel values based on the number of good pixels, ensuring effective noise reduction while preserving crucial image features. Comprehensive experiments on diverse image datasets, featuring varying noise levels, substantiate the superior performance of our fuzzy-based method in comparison to existing denoising techniques. The method not only outperforms in terms of quantitative metrics but also exhibits visually appealing results. Its adaptability is demonstrated across different scenarios, making it a robust solution for real-world applications where accurate image analysis hinges on noise-free data.

articleTitle: Health Monitoring System Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper consists of a healthcare system in an Internet of Things environment, which aims to monitor patient's health signs. The system consists of sensors to capture data from the hospital. The data is gathered with the help of a heart rate sensor, a body temperature sensor, a carbon monoxide sensor, a room temperature sensor, and a carbon dioxide sensor. The integration of all sensors into the IoT, the system enables continuous monitoring of patients' vital signs. This provides the help for the detection of any abnormal health conditions or unfavorable room conditions in early stage. The developed scheme maintains a low error percentage, ensuring the accuracy and reliability of the system. The error percentage is kept within a certain limit, which is specified to be less than 5%. This indicates that the system performs effectively in capturing and transmitting the sensor data.

articleTitle: Small Signal Analysis and Control of a Non-Isolated High gain Boost Converter for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The small signal modeling analysis and simulation in closed loop for the non-isolated high voltage gain converter are presented in this study. The operating point of power converter can be found with the use of the DC-DC converter's small signal analysis. The small signal analysis is explained in detail and it is used to calculate the various transfer functions relating input and output variables. A PI controller is used to regulate the converter's output in presence of load disturbance based on proportional integral (PI) control strategy. The simulation results for closed loop control are shown for a gain of approximately ten times. The effectiveness of the controller is also depicted by the simulation results showing servo and regulatory performances

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Nanowire FET & Internal Gate Nanowire FET
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In the context of scaling CMOS devices, various geometries have been proposed. This research examines the performance comparison between a standard 5-nm gate length Nanowire Field Effect Transistor (NWFET) and an NWFET with an Internal Gate. The study evaluates key parameters such as on-state current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>), off-state current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf>), Subthreshold Swing (SS), Drain Induced Barrier Lowering (DIBL), and I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> ratios to assess the performance of these devices. Notably, the investigation focuses on the impact of incorporating an inner gate within the structure. This inner gate structure exhibits lower SS and DIBL values, indicating enhanced control and improved short-channel behavior. The exceptional electrical performance of the internal gate design underscores its potential to augment subthreshold properties, thereby facilitating further advancements in device scaling.

articleTitle: A Thermoelectric Energy Harvesting System for Environmental Monitoring in WSN and IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Clean Energy harvesting is getting important in the last decade due to global warming and other pollutant effects. Researchers and Scientists are working to develop clean energy sources which can provide energy without spreading the pollution in the environment. Energy sources like batteries and cells are also the source of pollution and ideally should not be used. So, a reliable source of energy without pollution is always in high demand for Internet of Things (IoT) and Wireless Sensor Network (WSN). In this paper, a new design is proposed which can convert solar thermal energy into electrical energy. A brick with Thermoelectric Generator (TEG) has been proposed with a special arrangement which can provide energy during day and nighttime. Phase Change Material (PCM) is also used to store the thermal energy of solar heat. A mathematical model is also developed to check the validity of the proposed model. The Model can develop in terms of Brick and can be used to generate energy for smart buildings based on IoT and WSN technologies. The proposed system can generate 4.8mW of output power with 90oC temperature difference. This power can provide energy to any WSN node.

articleTitle: Positional Analysis and Comparison of Different Charge Generation Layer Based Blue OLEDs
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper includes three blue OLED devices which are D1, D2 and D3 where D1 is a non-CGL (charge generation layer) device, and D2 and D3 are CGL based devices. In all the devices, the CGL contains two materials 1.,4.,5.,8.,9.,11-hexaazatriphenylene-hexacarbonitrile (HAT -CN) and 1.,1-bis[(di-4-tolyamino)phenyl)]cyclohexane (TAP C) which act as electron and hole generators, respectively. As CGL provides additional charge carriers to D2 and D3 devices, these devices exhibit noteworthy improvement on the basis of luminescence and current. Among all the three devices, D3 shows the best performance. The luminescence of D3 is 2112.2 cd/m2 which is 10 times and 1.3 times enhanced in comparison with D1 and D2, correspondingly. Additionally, the current of D3 is 0.256 A which is 10 times and 1.4 times higher on comparing with D1 and D2, respectively. Moreover, the internal analysis of the devices is also performed using cutline and structure-based analysis to understand the in-depth performance improvements of D1, D2 and D3. The reported CGL based devices are useful for bio-medical and sensor applications.

articleTitle: Investigating the Influence of Timer Forecasting on Transmission Efficiency of TCP Connections in Dense Muli-Hop Wi-Fi Links
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Multi-hopping remains an effective solution in wireless scenarios with highly populated user strength. The internet protocol, especially the transmission control protocol (TCP) protocol, plays a huge role in the performance of systems with wireless links. The performance of TCP is heavily dependent upon the working of its timers. The TCP implementation largely trusts the retransmission timeout (RTO) timer algorithm that forecasts the packet delivery duration on a network connection. In multi-hop Wi-Fi links, RTO forecasting tumbles during impulsive round-trip time (RTT), which arises due to intermediate node re-routing and MAC retransmission. This experimental study intends to assess the effectiveness of different RTO algorithms and their impact on TCP connection transmission efficiency and latency characteristics in multi-hop Wi-Fi links. From the analysis at higher hop counts, CC-RTO obtained 35.12% and 17.2% by hybrid RTO. This study also examines the RTO's limits, like lack of accuracy in RTO estimation, and provides suggestions for lowering forecast errors in multi-hop Wi-Fi environments.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of SAW Sensor in COMSOL Multiphysics for Detection of Hexanal in Exhaled Breath
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Lung cancer remains a widespread health problem worldwide and maintains a dismal position as the leading cause of cancer deaths. The disease continues to claim significant lives, surpassing other cancers in mortality in both men and women. Considering this alarming reality, it is urgent to explore innovative diagnostic methods that can detect lung cancer in its early stages. The study of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) present in exhaled breath (EX) has emerged as a promising avenue to demonstrate their potential as biomarkers for various lung diseases. One particularly notable metabolic process contributing to this area is the peroxidation of unsaturated fatty acids, which results in the formation of a variety of volatile organic compounds, including aldehydes. Cancer cells, especially lung cancer, exhibit elevated levels of reactive oxygen species, which promote random lipid peroxidation and subsequent formation of various aldehydes. It is important to note that a significant portion of these volatile aldehydes are excreted from the body, which is why they are of interest as potential markers for early disease detection. Gas evaluation, especially the detection of low-concentration compounds such as hexanal, requires the development of highly accurate sensors. Therefore, we chose surface acoustic wave (SAW) sensors, which are known for their gas detection accuracy. The complex process involves designing and modeling the SAW sensor using COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2. The adsorption rate and conductivity of the gas sensor are determined based on the electric potential and the frequency response is examined at various eigen frequencies. Based on the results obtained, subsequent steps include further characterization and fabrication of a biosensor designed to detect volatile organic compounds (VOCs), which will enable the analysis of human exhaled air.

articleTitle: Early Forest Fire Prediction System Using Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Wireless sensor network (WSN), is a collection of sensors that is used for monitoring the activities in a given environment. They are used in the forests for fire detection wherea large number of sensor nodes are placed to detect the fire inits early stages. Forest fires are the main reason which affect the wildlife and many living creatures. The project performs a comparative analysis between the traditional system and the new system developed used to predict forest fires early using the Wireless sensor network for detecting forest fires with the goal of monitoring the scale and intensity of the wildfire ignited at forests. The solution involves deploying the fire sensing sensors across the forest area, calculating Fire Whether Index (FWI) of the regions, establishing data communications between the sensors using the protocol to create dynamic routing paths across the Wireless Sensor Network [7]. These paths are developed based on several factors such as fire, energy, weather index and security. Tracing the multi dynamic route is established using star topology where the red alert zones send the alert message to all the nearby base stations. Using Net Logo simulator this project analyses the performance of the traditional systems and new systems based on network power, fire detection efficacy and the overall power consumed by the fires alerting systems.

articleTitle: Ultrawide band High Gain Inset Feed Simple Structure in Patch Antenna for Sub 6-Ghz Application
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: An inset feed microstrip patch antenna for the ultrawide band is designed, simulated, fabricated, and analyzed in this paper. In order to accommodate sub-6 GHz 5G applications, the antenna is intended to operate at 5.5 GHz. The substrate used for the antenna fabrication and design is Rogers's 5880, which has a thickness of 1.57 mm and a permittivity of 2.2. With an inset feed of 50 Ω line, a straightforward rectangular patch serves as the antenna model. The antenna size is 49 x 49 mm2 overall. The simulation results show that the antenna exhibits a return loss of -15 dB at 1.6 GHz, and -21.6 dB at 5.8 GHz, and a gain of 1.0 dBi at 1.6GHz and 5.7 dBi at 5.5 GHz. measured results are in relatively good agreement which show that the antenna provides a gain of 1.2 dBi at 1.6 and 5.4dbi at 5.5 GHz and return loss of -20 dB at 1.6 GHz, and -28 dB at 5.5 GHz, A parametric analysis is also carried out to demonstrate the impacts of various parameters on the antenna's performance, offering useful recommendations for the design and operation of the antenna. The suggested antenna shows promise and can be an excellent choice for 5G applications operating at sub-6 GHz.

articleTitle: Wearable Dual Band Antenna Design for ISM band and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A novel dual-band wearable antenna designed to operate within the frequency bands of 2-4.42 GHz and 5.61-14.56 GHz is being proposed. This antenna employs a ground structure featuring symmetrical semicircular slots, which contribute to its enhanced performance. The antenna, shaped like a circle with rectangular slots, is strategically chosen to optimize the current path and improve antenna efficiency. The feeding mechanism utilizes microstrip feed technology to provide power to the radiator. With a compact size of 50mm×42mm×1.6mm and constructed using a polyamide substrate, the antenna is suitable for wearable applications. Despite its small form factor, the antenna achieves a peak gain of 7.28 dBi, making it a viable option for various communication scenarios. Extensive analysis and simulations have been conducted to evaluate the antenna's gain and radiation pattern, demonstrating its effectiveness in practical use cases. Overall, this proposed dual-band wearable antenna offers promising performance characteristics for ISM band and wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: MiraiBotGuard: Federated Learning for Intelligent Defense Against Mirai Threats
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: With the advancement of technology information has taken the shape of digital information that can belong to industries, businesses and other organizations. The information can be breached with various types of attacks and Internet of Things devices are widely used as equipment to target the victim machine which is storing the critical information. Artificial Intelligence-based methods have become frequent in providing cybersecurity solutions to the masses. The issue that arises with artificial intelligence methods is the need to share internal network logs with third-party or learning models. In this research work, the Mirai attack detection methodology is proposed using the federated learning approach with the deep neural network. The proposed model is evaluated using the CIC-IoT 2023 dataset by filtering network traffic related to the Mirai attack dataset. Further, the approach is evaluated for two scenarios covariate shift and concept drift. The local and global learning is enhanced using the federated averaging technique. The evaluation results are compared and studied based on metrics of accuracy, loss, precision and recall. The robustness and reliability of the proposed approach are proved with consistently improved results for state metrics and also the performance for concept drift outperforms the covariate shift.

articleTitle: Low Power and 72dB High Gain Op-Amp Design in $0.18\ \mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Design of a general purpose two stage Miller compensated Operational Amplifier (Op-Amp) using 180nm CMOS technology has been presented in this paper. The presented design offers a high dc gain of 72dB, Unity Gain Bandwidth of 51MHz for a large load capacitance of 1 pF and Phase Margin of nearly 60° while consuming a small power of nearly <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$280\mu\mathrm{W}$</tex>. In addition, our Op-Amp offers a CMRR of nearly 80dB, PSRR of greater than 85dB, Slew Rate (SR) of greater than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30\mathrm{V}/\mu^{\mathrm{s}}$</tex> and Input Common Mode Range (ICMR) of 0.53V – 1.37V. Simulation results show that the proposed Op-Amp offers a potential used in the design of voltage regulator, active filter, comparator and data converters etc.

articleTitle: Design and Investigation of Charge Plasma Based NCFET on MFIS and MFMIS Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this research paper, MFIS (Metal Ferroelectric Insulator Semiconductor) and MFMIS (Metal Ferroelectric Metal Insulator Semiconductor) structures are used to investigate a charge plasma based negative capacitance junctionless transistor. The devices are protected from the random dopant fluctuation by the charge plasma produced charge carriers, resulting in a steady threshold voltage. For both topologies, a thorough TCAD investigation of the influence of channel length scaling over short-channel effects (SCEs) is presented. In contrast to MFIS, where the fringing field impact is restricted to the channel region only, the inside metal layer makes the MFMIS structure exhibits significant increment in threshold voltage (VT), reductions in sub threshold swing (SS), and reduced DIBL. The effect of channel length scaling over SCEs are given and compared for both configurations using TCAD simulations.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Selection Combiner Under Different Wireless Mobile Fading Channels-A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper explores essential parameters in Large-Scale and Small-Scale fading in wireless mobile communication. Small-Scale fading, represented by the Nakagami-m model, and Large-Scale fading, involving Log-Normal Shadowing, are analyzed. The study evaluates the performance of Selection Combining (SC) under dual-branch diversity, providing a closed-form Mean Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) Gain expression. This enables a comparative analysis of Small-Scale and Large-Scale fading, offering insights into complex multipath shadowed environments. Additionally, it underscores the advantages of combining techniques in enhancing channel quality within real-world fading scenarios.

articleTitle: An Approach for Enhancement of Low Contrast Gray Scale Image Using Fuzzy Logic and Sigmoid Function
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Contrast enhancement plays a pivotal role in image processing, particularly for improving the visual quality of images in various applications. This paper presents an approach for enhancing such images by employing a point processing with the combination of Gaussian membership function for fuzzification and sigmoid function for modification. First, the image is fuzzified using Gaussian membership functions to transform pixel intensities into fuzzy sets, allowing for a more robust representation of the image's underlying characteristics. This fuzzification process effectively captures the uncertainty associated with pixel values in low contrast regions. Subsequently, a sigmoid function is applied to the fuzzified image to modify the pixel intensities. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method in enhancing low contrast images, as evidenced by significant improvements in visual quality and quantitative metrics such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and entropy. The proposed approach offers a promising solution for enhancing low contrast images across various applications, contributing to advancements in image processing and analysis.

articleTitle: Ensemble Transfer Learning Techniques for Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder is a complex neurological condition, becomes evident in children during the initial three years of their lives, Significantly influencing social dynamics, communication patterns, and behavioral norms. In this study, we introduce an ensemble learning-based classification model utilizing sMRI data to differentiate between control and Autism patients in the ABIDE dataset. The proposed method for precise categorization of Autism Spectrum Disorder relies significantly on the pivotal role of Convolutional Neural Networks. We utilize three pre-trained models, namely Vggl9, Densenetl21, and Mobilenetv2, which have been fine-tuned through transfer learning to optimize their performance. The evaluation process incorporates ensemble weighted averaging, and grid search optimization is applied to enhance the effectiveness of these models. The synergy of ensemble weighted averaging and grid search optimization proves to be highly effective, resulting in a 97% accuracy, 100% precision, 100% recall, 97% Fl-score, 97% specificity and 96% AUC score when validated using the ABIDE Dataset. This achievement signifies a noteworthy 1 % improvement over the accuracy attained by the best-performing individual model.

articleTitle: Quantum Encrypted Messaging Application: Harnessing Quantum Mechanics for Secure Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This research aims to develop a quantum encrypted messaging application that uses the principles of quantum mechanics to provide secure and privacy communication between users This project focuses on using quantum encryption techniques to improve messaging application security. The application will incorporate post-quantum algorithms to establish secure communication channels, ensuring that messages exchanged between users are protected from eavesdropping and unauthorized access Messaging application exit results will provide users with greater security and a quantum-resistant platform for private transactions -Will address the emerging need for quantum-secure encryption in this era of threats

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Low Power Oximeter
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The monitoring of pulse rate and oxygen saturation stands as pivotal clinical metrics indicative of essential physiological processes. Oxygen saturation denotes the concentration of oxygenated hemoglobin within arterial blood, offering insights into blood oxygenation levels. Utilizing light-emitting diodes (LEDs) and photo detectors, pulse oximeters offer an economical and non-intrusive method for tracking both pulse rate and blood oxygen saturation. The objective of this project is to develop an innovative electronic circuit integrating an analog filter to effectively isolate red and green photoplethysmography (PPG) data. The project entails building and implementing a tiny micro controller-based portable system using available optoelectronic sensors and PPG. This system is specialized to measuring, displaying, and confirming finger-based heart rate measurements. The averaged heart rate values are then shown on a text-based LCD screen, which refreshes every ten seconds. The development concept shows promise for a variety of healthcare applications, demonstrating its ability to improve health monitoring procedures.

articleTitle: Implementation of Low Powered CMOS Potentiostat in Biomedical Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Continuous blood glucose monitoring has been demonstrated in recent research to dramatically lessen the symptoms of diabetes. The “Wireless Implantable Microsystem for Continuous Blood Glucose Monitoring,” also known as the “implant,” proves to overcome problems such as painful needle sticks, irregular assessments and numerous trips to doctor's clinic and aims at improving the well-being of individuals with diabetes. This project focuses on software implementation of Continuous Glucose Monitoring system and optimizing it by integrating a low-powered CMOS potentiostat and minimizing the sensor size. This design allows for implantation just beneath the skin, enabling contact with blood from capillaries or interstitial fluid. This approach holds promise for long-term continuous glucose monitoring, addressing the limitations of current methods and enhancing the overall management of diabetes. It is designed using 0.18-µm CMOS technology with a full-scale measurable current of upto 0.95 µA and a supply voltage of 1.2 V.

articleTitle: A Soft Computing Approach for Efficient Diagnosis of Otitis Media Infection by Mucosal Disease Early Detection and Referrals
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Otitis Media (OM) represents a prevalent and potentially severe middle ear condition, primarily affecting children. Timely and accurate OM diagnosis is crucial for effective intervention. Often it happens due to mucosal diseases affected by mucosal membranes. This study explores the application of deep learning techniques to tympanic membrane (TM) images for precise OM detection. the dataset, collected and verified from AIIMS Raipur Hospital, comprises four distinct image categories: Chronic Otitis Media (COM), Earwax plug (EP), Myringosclerosis (MS), and normal Tympanic Membrane (TM). Each category encompasses 40 meticulously selected images for training and 40 for testing. Binary and multi-class classification 3-layer models were developed and rigorously assessed using standard performance metrics, including accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and Fl-score. The binary classification models consistently demonstrated impressive accuracy, surpassing 95%, in distinguishing various OM types from normal TMs. Notably, the COM vs. Normal model achieved an accuracy of 97.03%. Furthermore, the multi-class classification model exhibited an overall accuracy of 89.45% for categorizing TMs into COM, EP, MS, and normal classes.

articleTitle: R-Peak Detection Using Wavelet Scattering Transform for Pre-Term Infant ECG Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Heart-related disease is one of the pre-eminent origins of mortality across the globe. Early and accurate detection of heart-related disease is essential to avoid an uncertain mishap. Peak detection is a pivotal step for the analysis of different spectral signals. The dislocation of peaks disrupts the detection accuracy of a heart-related disease. This study proposes a method for accurate R-peak detection of ECG signal. The acute R-peak detection of ECG signal is achieved using wavelet scattering transform. It eliminates the artifacts associated to signal with the help of inbuilt filters, proves reliable as it identifies the R-peaks at correct location. The wavelet scattering transform generates rational, instructive, and invariable translation representation of signals. The efficiency of the proposed method for R-peak detection is evaluated on pre-term infant ECG dataset available at physionet. The attained average accuracy and specificity for R-peak detection is 99.23% and 99.86% respectively. The proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods namely continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and thresholding technique.

articleTitle: Improved Implementation of PYNQ-Based FFT Hardware Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In recent times, the idea of hardware accelerators has gained a lot of attraction, which are implemented on Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) to speed-up the com-monly used software functions. The interest increased even more when Xilinx released Python Productivity for Zynq (PYNQ), a framework offering a much easier design methodology for such accelerators. In this study, we have designed a hardware accel-erator for a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) filter using PYNQ. The performance of the designed accelerator is compared with its already available software implementation in the Numerical Python (NumPy) library and with published designs on FFT filter accelerators that used custom-designed Direct Memory Access (DMA) Intellectual Property (IP). However, customizing the IPs requires a lot of specialization in various areas, such as architecture, low-level programming, API development, etc. Therefore, in this research, we have used standard DMA IP available in Vivado along with run-time non-configurable (i.e. fixed size) FFT to show that one can still achieve a high speed-up, or even more and lesser hardware utilization (%) using smart design choices. The technique to employ that fixed size FFT design for different input sample sizes during run time is also explained in the paper. The results for delay, resources, and power consumption for different sample sizes are then shown and compared, which will aid in choosing the platform for computing FFT and designing such accelerators accordingly.

articleTitle: A 14T Radiation Resistant Self-Recoverable SRAM Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Space radiation malfunctions electric circuits are particularly vulnerable to memory device's sensitive storage nodes and disrupts stored data. Standard 6T SRAM cannot mitigate this interruption. Consequently, multiple authors suggested resilience solutions. However, there is a compromise between the performance of the memory cells and the likelihood of soft errors. This work explores the SR-14T, a polar design self recoverable SRAM memory cell, which efficiently recovers lost data from high-energy particle strikes. SR-14T outperforms its performance in read stability, hold power dissipation, write access time, and effective critical charge even at VDD and temperature variations. The proposed SR-14T additionally attains a superior overall performance to address the trade-off problem.

articleTitle: Link Loss Identification and Congestion-Aware Routing in Mobile Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Mobile Wireless Sensor Networks (MWSNs) are self-possessed of movable nodes transmitting via the wireless medium, absent any permanent infrastructure. In MWSN, link loser is an essential concern owing to the motion of the nodes, which creates network congestion. Congestion happens in any in-between nodes while data packets journey from sender to receiver as well as they acquire high packet drop also lengthy delay that induces the function degradations. To overcome these problems in this paper, Link Loss identification and Congestion-Aware (LLCA) routing in MWSN is proposed. This approach identifies the congestion based on computing node Queue conditions in the network. This mechanism chooses the forwarder node based on residual energy, link grade and congestion factor; therefore exerting the capability to determine unfailing routes. Here, the link loser identification method for forecast the present link condition to evade link loser as well as minimize the packet drop. The simulation results illustrated that the introduced approach diminishes the packet loss rate and enhance the network throughput in the network.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Routing Protocol Performance for Enhanced Operations of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are airborne nodes that are controlled remotely from ground stations. They have been used in a variety of applications in recent years, including disaster management, military operations, search and rescue, ecological study, and others. Among the advancements, the notion of Flying Ad-hoc Networks (FANETs) stands out. FANET, functions remotely like Mobile Ad-hoc Networks (MANETs) and Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs), are an advancement over standard networking systems. Ad-hoc networks are necessary for both civilian and military operations, demanding a variety of support systems. In Ad-hoc Networks, data is always sent under all situations, which is required for seamless communication across all UAVs. In contrast, the complex dynamics and ever-changing topology of UAV networks make it difficult for researchers to integrate efficient routing procedures into FANETs. The accomplishment of UAV routing procedures is related to the total network's success rate. Producing a routing system capable of cost- effective and reliable data transfer in such a difficult environment is a difficult assuming. In this study, we look at routing protocols using the NS3 simulator. In this research, we investigate routing protocols using the NS3 simulator. The study looks at the effectiveness of several UAV routing protocols, including Ad-Hoc On-Demand Distance Vector (AODV), Destination Sequenced Distance Vector (DSDV), and Optimized Link State Routing (OLSR). These protocols' performance is evaluated using a variety of measures, including Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), Packet Loss Ratio (PLR), Throughput, End-to-End Delay, and Jitter Delay. The findings estimation the effectiveness of routing processes in the presence of varying UAV speeds. This research carefully explores how different routing protocols function under varied UAV intensities and speeds.

Index Terms: Speed Of The Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
Author Keywords: Flying Ad hoc Network Performance Analysis

articleTitle: Implementation of Pruned and Quantized Semantic Segmentation Neural Network Using Cambridge-Driving Labeled Video Database (CamVid) Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In This research investigates the streamlined implementation of Semantic Segmentation Neural Networks through advanced techniques: pruning and quantization. Leveraging the CamVid dataset, our study achieved remarkable reductions in computational complexity and memory usage. Pruning removed redundant connections, effectively reducing learnable parameters, while quantization significantly minimized memory footprint. Despite these optimizations, the networks maintained high semantic segmentation accuracy. The implications of our findings are pivotal, particularly in resource-constrained applications like autonomous driving and image analysis. By enhancing efficiency without compromising accuracy, this research facilitates the seamless integration of deep learning models into real-time systems. Our study not only advances the field of computer vision but also underscores the practical feasibility of deploying sophisticated neural networks in practical, resource-efficient contexts.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Diagnostic Accuracy of Colon Diseases Using Multi-Class Classification Technique and Endoscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Colon diseases are a significant health concern worldwide, with conditions such as polyps, esophagitis, and ulcerative diseases posing substantial risks to patients. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment and prevention of complications. In recent years, deep learning techniques have shown promising results in the field of medical image analysis, offering the potential to enhance the diagnostic process. In this research, a transfer learning-based Inception V3model is proposed for the multi-classification of colon disease using endoscopic images. This study focuses on the classification of four major classes: Normal, Polyps, Esophagitis, and Ulcerative diseases. The dataset used for this research comprises a diverse collection of endoscopic images obtained from online platforms. The training process involves the optimization of hyperparameters such as optimizers namely Adam and Adadelta, with batch size 32 and 100 epochs to enhance the robustness of the model. The proposed classification system has obtained the highest value of validation accuracy as 93.65% on the Adam optimizer. The proposed system holds great promise for assisting clinicians in the early diagnosis and classification of colon diseases, thereby facilitating timely intervention.

articleTitle: Automatic Fabric Defect Detection using Deep CNN-AlexNet Models
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Defect detection stands as a pivotal quality control measure within the realm of manufacturing. Recent studies have witnessed the successful implementation of defect detection systems across diverse domains, ranging from scrutinizing steel surfaces to assessing fruit grades, and notably, integrating these systems into smart factories. In textile manufacturing, the automated identification of fabric defects has become indispensable, given the intricate nature of fabric textures, where minute imperfections can easily elude human perception. Consequently, relying solely on human inspection proves inadequate for resolving these challenges. Moreover, there has been a notable upswing of interest in applying IoT and machine learning techniques to bolster defect detection processes, owing to their demonstrated reliability. Consequently, the pursuit of defect detection has shifted towards a foundation rooted in Deep Learning. The core objective of this paper revolves around honing fabric defect detection through the utilization of CNN, a renowned deep learning model. This research utilizes CNN based pretrained models for fabric defeat prediction. It takes the popular AlexNet pretrained models for fabric defeat prediction on AITEX Fabric Image Set. The experimental results show that AlexNet provide a good accuracy 93.4% compared with normal CNN model.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Power of Deep Learning in Brain Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Brain tumors represent a substantial source of morbidity and mortality on a global scale. Early Identification and precise diagnosis are crucial for successful treatment outcomes. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) has become a cornerstone in the diagnosis of brain tumors, but interpreting these scans is time-consuming and requires significant expertise. Deep Learning (DL) & Image Processing Techniques offer promising solutions to this problem. This project introduces a DL-based approach for identifying brain tumors from MRI scans. The proposed approach involves image preprocessing, feature extraction & classification using supervised ML Algorithms, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). The method involves preprocessing the MRI scans using various techniques, including filtering and segmentation, to remove noise and highlight potential tumor regions and extract features from the preprocessed images, such as texture, shape, and intensity using various image processing Techniques. These features are then used to train and test the DL models, which predict whether an MRI scan contains a tumor or not. Evaluation of the proposed approach on a large dataset of MRI scans collected from patients with brain tumors and healthy individuals substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed method in precisely identifying brain tumors. The CNN models demonstrate notable levels of accuracy & sensitivity, indicating their potential for use in Clinical settings. The project carries significant potential to advance the early detection and diagnosis of brain tumors, there by contributing to better patient outcomes and a reduction in mortality rates.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of FSK and GFSK Modulation Techniques for an Underwater Wireless Acoustic Modem
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Underwater Wireless Communication systems deployed by the military helps build a strong marine defense security of a nation state. An Underwater Acoustic Modem (UAM) is the heart of the Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (U-WSN). Various UAMs employ CDMA Spread spectrum based FSK modulation for data transmission. However it suffers multipath reflections besides possessing higher susceptibility to noise along with limited bandwidth in the acoustic environment both of which together contribute to a higher BER and consequently lower data rates. GFSK modulation, on the other hand leads to higher data rates because of its higher Power Spectral Density (PSD) and higher spectral efficiency compared to FSK modulation. The simulations of both the modulation schemes have been done using MATLAB 15.0. The comparative analysis of FSK and GFSK modulation for two UAMs separated by a distance of 150cm over an AWGN channel followed by the two path Rayleigh fading channel has concluded a lower BER and higher PSD in case of both the UAMs using GFSK modulation.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Versatile Drone for Multi-Payload Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The paper presents the innovative design and development of a versatile, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) optimized for multi-payload applications, with an emphasis on agricultural crop disease detection. The drone is equipped with a variety of sensors such as high-definition video cameras, gyroscopes, and GPS, which makes it easier to integrate different payloads customized for particular applications. An important aspect of the proposed UAVis its integration of machine learning technology, specifically a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), for the real-time analysis and identification of crop diseases from aerial images. This method promises to revolutionize agricultural practices by enabling precise, early detection of diseases, thereby minimizing crop losses and optimizing yields. The paper provides the construction of the drone, including material selection for durability and weight optimization. It also outlines the machine learning pipeline, from data collection and model training to real-time deployment on the drone for in-field analysis. The results demonstrate the UAV's capability to successfully identify crop diseases, which shows its potential for broader applications in surveillance, delivery, and environmental monitoring. YOLO (You Only Look Once) is an advanced object detection algorithm renowned for its real-time performance and high accuracy. Unlike conventional methods that detect objects in multiple stages, YOLO employs a single convolutional neural network (CNN) to simultaneously predict bounding boxes and class probabilities. This approach enables rapid and precise object detection in images and videos, making it ideal for applications requiring fast processing, such as surveillance, autonomous vehicles, and drone operations.

articleTitle: Enhancing Disaster Recovery Mechanism in SCADA using Multichain Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The disaster recovery mechanism is employed in various industries but in critical infrastructure scenarios, the process should be reliable and resilient. This research paper proposes a novel framework for disaster recovery methods for as Supervisory control and data acquisition systems using communication channels created by blockchain technology. The permission blockchain technology is integrated with as Supervisory control and data acquisition devices for configuring the data and event-sharing techniques. The research work presents the process of configuring and implementing the disaster recovery process of risk assessment, backup creation and event logging. Further, the events in the critical infrastructure are controlled by smart contract automation as part of the multichain blockchain. The consensus for fault tolerance is achieved by keeping 90% of the nodes operational in the network. The proposed solution is simulated by creating a private communication channel among as Supervisory control and data acquisition devices and the performance is evaluated with successful execution rate and average time of block confirmation by the disaster recovery process. The mining diversity, number of required active nodes, creation of stream and creation of distributed ledger is controlled by single administrative node in the proposed architecture which can be configured according to the requirements of the SCADA network architecture.

articleTitle: Design of Digitized Visual Search Task for Assessment of Aging Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Mild cognitive impairments (MCI) develop in adults due to the normal aging process and may sometimes progress to a more serious cognitive decline stage resulting in Dementia. If the cognitive decline is identified at the MCI stage, it can be delayed or prevented from progressing by different interventions. A typical indicator of cognitive impairments that might be caused due to an injury, aging, or other factors is found to be a decreased search efficiency in visual search tasks. Here we propose a model to assess this efficiency by designing a digitized, easy-to-use visual search task capable of incorporating multiple variables in the visual stimulus, affecting the search capabilities. The variables under consideration include the number of distracting elements, target size, target distance from the center of the stimulus area, and habituation effects. This designed stimulus is tested on participants from different age groups.

articleTitle: Investigation of Retransmission Timeout Forecasting in Multihop Wireless Links
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The retransmission timeout (RTO) algorithm predicts the packet transmission duration between end-to-end devices. The faulty RTO timeout occurrence in vehicular links tumbles timer predictions during delayed acknowledgment (ACK) due to impulsive round-trip time (RTT) delay. The modified timer projection RTO (MTP-RTO) implementation uses a novel approach incorporating dynamic weights and additional timer variables that significantly reduce faulty timeouts. The MTP-RTO forecasting algorithm outperforms contemporary RTO approaches in in-vehicle networks by achieving the best RTO-RTT deviation, improving transmission efficiency and latency performance.

articleTitle: Design of an Optimal IIR Full-Band Digital Differentiator
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this paper a novel metaheuristic algorithm called the Coati optimization algorithm (COA) is used to design a 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order infinite impulse response (IIR) full-band digital differentiator (DD) by optimizing the filter coefficients. The objective is to closely approximate the frequency response of the proposed filter so that it tries to meet the ideal frequency response characteristics of an ideal differentiator. COA is a population-based metaheuristic algorithm which imitates the natural behavior of coatis when they are attacking iguanas and evading from predators. Every member of the coati's population represents a possible optimal solution based on their positions in the search space. The COA based design of the IIR DD is compared with various other designs obtained with traditional algorithms and proved to be better in terms of various error performance parameters. Overall, these improved results for the proposed filter can become an inspiration for various digital signal processing applications.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Aspect Category Detection for Hindi Data Using TF-IDF and Count Vectorization
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Sentiment is related to emotions. The emergence of e-commerce has initiated a novel trend in the realm of natural language processing, mainly through sentiment analysis applied to user-generated reviews. Hindi, as an Indian language, is utilized by many users. With the remarkable surge in online product reviews in Hindi, there has also been a rapid increase in post-web Hindi reviews. Aspect-based sentiment analysis comprises aspect category detection (ACD) and addresses the challenge of assigning a specific review sentence to a predefined set of aspect categories. In this task, it's important that a single review sentence can potentially be associated with one or more of these predefined categories. In this paper, machine learning-based transformation approaches for aspect category detection are examined on a well-accepted Hindi data set. This is based on a multi-label classification paradigm. Term-frequency / Inverse-Document Frequency (TF-IDF) and count vectorization algorithms are used for feature extraction. A range of evaluation parameters, including as precision, recall, F1-score, and Hamming Loss, are included in the results. In every case, the logistic regression (LR) classifier consistently generated the most pertinent and relevant results.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Tunnel: A Review of Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Tunnel Field Effect Transistors (TFETs) bear a distinct advantage over other transistors: they exhibit extremely low quiescent currents, which can be as low as picoamperes. The three key variables that influence the characteristics of TFETs are the attainment of high Ion current, restriction of subthreshold slope value, and reduction of ambipolar leakage. Compared to MOSFETs, TFETs exhibit superior transconductance per bias current, owing to their SS decrease of less than 60 mV per decade. This article presents a comprehensive analysis of various TFET device architectures and their associated performances. The study delves into numerous TFET device topologies and scrutinizes the efficacy of each design in producing the desired Ion/Ioff ratios.

articleTitle: Enabling Seamless Mobility in 5G NR Networks Using NS-3 and 4G Core Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper proposes the integration of 5G New Radio (5G NR) with a 4G core network, specifically focusing on its implications for voice call applications. The main goal is to create a smooth link between a current 4G core network and a distant device, showcasing how 5G NR can revolutionize modern communication systems. Expected results include much faster data speeds, noticeable decreases in delays, and an overall better connection. To achieve this, we use simulation with Network Simulator-3 (NS3), to analyze the integration process to control the packet losses. NS3 plays a crucial role in our project by helping us create realistic models and simulate various scenarios. we can assess the network's performance in a more robust way under various conditions. Our work provides practical insights into the adaptability and advantages of 5G technology in different applications. It highlights the importance of futuristic network architectures. Our work serves as a valuable resource in advancing communication technologies, bridging the gap between theory and the practical implementation of 5G NR into existing 4G core networks.

articleTitle: A Survey on Artificial Intelligence-Based Cyber Security in IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: With the growth of network technologies and the increase in data transmission, cyber threats have become more complicated. Artificial Intelligence allows automated detection of cyber-attacks, which is important for IoT security. To achieve this, this research examines the application of deep learning and machine learning methods to DoS protection strategies for the IoT. The study uses performance metrics, and validation methods to stimulate further research on IoT security and intrusion detection systems using ensemble learning. The objective of this study was to explore and enhance the present state of knowledge regarding IoT Security, as well as to produce intrusion detection systems employing ensemble learning. We conducted a comprehensive survey of existing literature by various authors, without undertaking any original experimentation.

articleTitle: Novel Multilevel Inverter with SPWM Control Technique for PV System Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Generally, conversion from fixed DC to variable AC require two stage conversion devices, due to this two stage conversion process the complexity of control of converter raising, more no of switching devices require, cost of converters increases and Total harmonic distortion (THD) having more. Based on the above drawbacks many researchers have been introduced various Multilevel inverters (MLI) which have (N-1) switching devices for N level inverter. Hence here a single stage conversion circuit of multilevel inverter (MLI) is proposed. it has ability to operate as five level inverter and seven level inverters with less semiconductor devices and the lower THD of an output equate to two stage conversion devices and other conventional MLIs. The controllability of the inverter can be implemented by concept of Sinusoidal Pulse width Modulation (SPWM) technique. The validity of the inverter can be evaluated based on fewer semiconductor devices, simple operation, less THD of an output voltage and current. Its functionality could potentially be verified with the MATLAB/Simulink tool.

articleTitle: Four-Port Multi-Ring-Based MIMO Antenna for Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A simple and efficient four-port multi-ring Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna is proposed. It is intended to function in the 2.77-19 GHz wideband region, which consists of the Ku-band (12–18 GHz), X (8.2-12 GHz), and ultra-wideband (UWB) (3.1-10.6 GHz) bands. This 60×60 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> antenna is developed on a FR4 substrate. Orthogonal placement of four antenna elements yields polarization diversity. At the center, the top substrate layer incorporates a Multi-Ring Decoupling Structure which improves isolation by more than 20 dB across the majority of operating bands. Thus, the antenna offered an impedance bandwidth of 16.23 GHz. Additionally, a peak gain of 6.8 dB and an efficiency ranging from 71 % to 94% are attained. The proposed MIMO antenna yielded improved MIMO diversity parameters, which include Mean Effective Gain, Diversity Gain, Total Active Reflection Coefficient, and Envelope Correlation Coefficient. The comparison of results demonstrated the novelty of the reported antenna with the recently reported MIMO antennas for the UWB and X-Ku-bands applications.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Health Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this paper, an IoT-based health monitoring system using Arduino proposed and developed focusing on developing pulse oximeter for measuring parameters like heart rate and oxygen concentration level in our body. All of us seen a covid-19 pandemic which make all of us think about how we can monitor general health parameter and its importance in keep us healthy. In all over world, the price of pulse oximeter raised and its was available in black market with approximately 400 times higher price. After paying that much amount it was not easy to get pulse oximeter. We developed a system which measured the heartbeat as Bpm and Blood oxygen concentration as SpO2. Along with these two parameters we measured the room temperature and humidity condition to study its impact on heartrate and blood oxygen levels. For studying its impact, we measured this for 200 people and fetched pattern among those parameters. A person's BMI has a major impact on his heart rate and blood oxygen levels concentration. Gender also has a key impact on Bpm and SpO2. From the study it has been also found that the majority of the person's Bpm lies in between 65 to 95 beats per minute and majority of the person has SpO2 in between 94 to 98 whereas ideal range of Bpm is 60 to 100 and for SpO2 is 93 to 100. We can see the impact of athletic habits medicine consumption in Bpm as well as SpO2.

Author Keywords: Heart rate and Blood oxygen concentration

articleTitle: Optimization of Spectrum Sensing in Cognitive Radio Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Spectrum sensing (SS) is the most significant and challenging task in the CR technique which identifies the availability of the spectral holes for opportunistic access. Spectrum sensing technique should ensure the reliable detection of the primary user signal in various scenarios like fading channels, Noise uncertainty and Hidden node problems. Recently ML technique is widely used in wireless communication applications. In this paper, ML based spectrum sensing scheme has been proposed, which enhances the detection accuracy under low SNR scenario while reducing the computational complexity involved in threshold computation required in conventional energy detection approach. ANN, SVM ML based approaches are used as a classical binary classifier to classify the received signal samples into two classes and subsequently provides the information about the presence of the primary user in the given band. Sensing performance is presented in terms of Probability of detection, accuracy and error rate as given in the simulation results.

articleTitle: Face Shape Microstrip Antenna for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
