abstract: This study introduces a novel microstrip antenna designed for UWB applications, featuring an elliptical-faced monopole patch with an integrated feed line. The antenna has a bandwidth from 2.9 - 11.9 GHz, considering Return Loss values below -10 dB. Fabricated on an FR-4 substrate with dimensions of 26mm x 26mm x 1.6mm, the substrate has a dielectric strength <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}})$</tex> of 4.7. The UWB antenna design was executed using CST Studio Suite Software, employing a transmission line model based on characteristic impedance. The investigation scrutinizes essential parameters such as substrate dimensions, feed size, and ground plane, aiming to understand their impact on the antenna's performance across the frequency domain.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Analysis of Power, Hardware, and Temperature Constraints in 4-Bit Full Adder Circuits for High-Speed Data Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Energy shortage is currently a serious problem in many developing countries. An energy-efficient 4-bit full adder that uses multiple FPGA families and the Xilinx Vivado software framework has been developed, leading to the evolution of environmentally conscious communication. Xilinx Vivado is used in the study to implement an energy-efficient design for communication devices with an emphasis on controlling temperature, power dissipation, and energy consumption. The suggested design combines effective hardware utilization with power-saving strategies to provide maximum energy efficiency. The study also looks into how temperature affects circuit performance and reliability, demonstrating the benefits and viability of energy-efficient design for communication hardware circuits. Energy conservation is achieved through this while comparing with the Virtex and Zynq board.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Credit Card Fraud Detection Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Because of the development and quick expansion of E-Commerce, the usage of credit cards for online purchases has skyrocketed, resulting in an explosion in credit card fraud. As credit cards become the most prominent means of payment for both digital and in-store purchases, the number of incidents of fraud related to them rises. In practical instances, determining whether a transaction is legitimate or fraudulent is a complicated and demanding undertaking. As a result, all credit card issuing organizations must implement robust fraud detection systems to prevent losses. This study attempts to compare different strategies and determine which one is the most efficient. This study used Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, Random Forests, K Nearest Neighbors and gradient boosting frameworks including Xgboost, LightGBM, and CatBoost Models are built using the European Dataset. The outcomes are analyzed using three parameters: precision, recall, and F1 score. This research aids in determining the most efficient algorithm among the many algorithms employed.

articleTitle: Design of RF Sensor for Human Neck Motion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this paper, a rectangular microstrip spiral patch antenna is designed, simulated and evaluated in a 2.45 GHz ISM band. Polydimethylsiloxane with a thickness of Imm is used as substrate. The suggested antenna is intended to test in both on-body and free space scenarios, with the goal of achieving a lower SAR than current antennas; it is also intended to track changes in neck position. Therefore, the reflection characteristics are analyzed. The SAR reached a peak SAR value of 0.133 when it was computed for open space and on-body conditions at 2.45 GHz frequency. Computer simulation technology (CST) has been used in the design and simulation of antenna. With this, our designed approach is useful for detecting ailments and provides information to the user for good posture.

articleTitle: Handcrafted Feature Assisted Light-Weight Encoder Decoder Based Classifier for Yoga Posture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The trend for the need for at-home workout regimens and the potential for technology to support the trend is rising as remote employment becomes more and more common. One such activity that has benefits like increased flexibility and stress alleviation is yoga. Presently, numerous self-guided yoga courses in the form of pictures and videos are available online. Consequently, there is an urgent requirement for a system that can recognize and evaluate the precision of yoga posture execution in these instructional materials. In the current scenario lightweight prediction models are very much essential because devices like smartphones, edge devices, and embedded systems that have limited processing power or battery life, lightweight models are the best option as they require less resources to train and operate. One particular approach of making the recognition system lightweight is the use of keypoint-based pose/action classifiers. In this paper, a lightweight classifier for yoga postures based on neural network architecture using MoveNet pose estimation technique is proposed. Our model is able to classify the yoga postures by learning the human joints information in a efficient manner.

articleTitle: Categorization of Brain Tumor on MR Images Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Convolution Neural Network (CNN) algorithms have demonstrated notable capability in effectively analyzing human body image datasets obtained from MRI or CT with sufficient efficiency to direct medical operations. Although clinicians and radiologists can adeptly detect the presence of tumors and general abnormalities in brain scans, differentiating between specific tumor types typically requires significant time and effort. This study introduces an approach employing CNN algorithms for precise brain tumor classification into four distinct classes, leveraging deep learning models such as ResNet-50 and InceptionV3.Prior to classification, the dataset undergoes preprocessing using Adaptive Median Filter (AMF) and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) for denoising and contrast enhancement. The classification task involves categorizing images into four classes namely Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary and Tumorless. The proposed methodology aims to streamline the analysis process by minimizing complexity while maximizing accuracy rates when compared to previous developments.

articleTitle: Autonomous Quadruped Robot Equipped with Obstacle Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The proposed work describes the design and features of a quadruped autonomous robot that includes advanced obstacle sensing technology. A quadrupedal robot with a four-legged design mimicking animal movement excels at navigating rough terrains. The robotic system is outfitted with a variety of sensors, including visible cameras and ultrasonic sensors, and has a sophisticated control system for immediate processing of environmental data. The obstacle detection technology utilised in the system guarantees efficient and safe navigation, allowing for immediate perception and adaptive responses to obstacles encountered. Utilising its quadrupedal structure, the robot showcases its ability to adapt to irregular terrain and navigate obstacles by making dynamic modifications in leg movements and stride. The incorporation of AI algorithms improves the robot's decision-making capabilities, letting it navigate complex environments independently, avoid obstacles, and determine the best pathways. The robotic platform has found applications in a variety of fields, including autonomous surveillance, industrial inspection, search and rescue missions, and exploration. These different use cases demonstrate the platform's versatility and cost-effectiveness, establishing it as a viable alternative for autonomous robotic systems operating in demanding situations.

articleTitle: Real-Time Object Recognition with Voice Feedback for Visually Impaired Based on Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Visually impaired individuals rely on real-time object recognition to overcome the challenges posed by their limited visual capabilities. Traditional navigation for the visually impaired often involves the use of canes or guide dogs, but these methods have limitations, particularly when it comes to identifying specific objects, obstacles, or changes in the environment. Real-time object recognition technology utilizes cameras and advanced algorithms to identify and interpret visual information in real-time, providing auditory or haptic feedback to users. This capability enables visually impaired individuals to access instant information about their surroundings, such as recognizing familiar objects, reading signs, avoiding obstacles, and navigating through complex environments independently. This technology enhances their spatial awareness and allows them to make informed decisions, promoting greater autonomy and reducing reliance on external assistance. Hence, in this work an efficient approach to address the challenges faced by visually impaired individuals through the development of a real-time object recognition system with voice feedback has been designed. The proposed system leverages the capabilities of Raspberry Pi, integrating computer vision techniques to identify objects in the surroundings. In real-time, the system processes live video input from a camera, identifies objects, and provides instant auditory feedback to the user through a voice interface. The proposed system accuracy and efficiency are evaluated through comprehensive testing, demonstrating its potential as an assistive technology to enhance the liberation and security of visually impaired users in home environments.

articleTitle: Flood Prediction System with Voting Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Flood prediction plays a vital role in reducing the influence of natural disasters among the communities and the infrastructure. This paper presents a machine learning approach for flood prediction using a voting classifier, combining information from turbidity, gauge height, and discharge as key features. The dataset, comprising historical records of these parameters, serves as the foundation for training and evaluating the predictive models. In our work, we employ a voting classifier, integrating Random Forest and Gradient Boosting algorithms to harness the strengths of diverse models. The ensemble approach aims to enhance prediction accuracy and robustness by aggregating the predictions of individual classifiers. The choice of features turbidity, gauge height, and discharge is motivated by their relevance in capturing hydrological dynamics associated with flood events. The dataset is preprocessed to handle missing values, normalize features, and encode the target variable. The voting classifier is being trained upon a subset of data, and its accomplishment is estimated on a discrete test set. Various metrics, including accuracy, are employed to assess the model's predictive capabilities. Results indicate promising performance in flood prediction, showcasing the potential of ensemble methods for such applications. This system assures an accuracy of about approx. 99% and alert notification will be sent to the residents of flood predicted areas. Hence, this contributes to the ongoing efforts in leveraging machine learning techniques and also provides an alert notification for enhancing disaster preparedness and response with proper communication.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for the Building Energy Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The construction industry consumes 35% of all global energy. Building energy conservation is critical for lowering emissions and consumption. Properly functioning the building's heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) unit helps to reduce energy consumption. Predicting building energy consumption with machine learning (ML) models can help to improve HVAC functionality. As a result, the performance of various ML predictive models based on k-nearest neighbor (KNN), artificial neural network (ANN), support vector regression (SVR), and Ridge and Lasso regression models is investigated in this work for the prediction of energy usage. Furthermore, Bayesian optimization for different random states (RS) is used to estimate the hyperparameters of the ML models that have been implemented. The results show that ANN performs best for RS values between 0 and 75. However, SVR achieves the lowest RMSE for RS, equal to 25, 50, 100, 150, and 200, compared to ANN, KNN, Ridge, and Lasso (RMSE=2.910), respectively. Finally, SVR predicts energy consumption more accurately than other designed models in most cases.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Classification With Jetson Nano
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia, or ALL, is a frequent, severe type of blood cancer that mainly affects young-sters.Classifying leukemia subtypes accurately and early is essential for enhancing patient outcomes and treatment planning. With the help of Jetson Nano, a small and potent edge computing platform, we present a novel method in this work for the automatic classification of ALL subtypes.Our system analyzes high-resolution microscopic images of blood samples taken from leukemia patients using deep learning techniques, notably convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Preprocessing techniques are applied to enhance image quality, and a customized CNN architecture is developed and optimized for the Jetson N ano platform. The model is instructed on a sizable dataset comprising diverse leukemia cell images, enabling it to learn intricate patterns and features associated with different ALL subtypes.

articleTitle: Fake Clones for Adversaries Detection with Efficient Relay Selection in MWSN
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Mobile Wireless Sensor Network (MWSN) is a new talented technology. Transmitting data from sender to receiver is a problematic concern since the stabilities of mobile nodes along this route are changeable in the wireless environment. In MWSN, energetic topography owing to the nodes being mobile and features like open configuration are endangered via several attacks. To defend perceptive data, it is essential to avert the adversary from violating and disclosing the position of the sender and receiver. This mechanism introduces Fake Clones for Adversaries Detection (FCAD) with efficient relay selection. The FCAD mechanism creates the public and private keys based on the Elliptic Curve Cryptography algorithm. It establishes the sender and receiver fake clone nodes to separate the adversaries efficiently. Furthermore, the Sand Cat Swarm Optimization (SCSO) process chooses a better relay node based on node mobility, energy, and delay. The simulation results illustrate that the FCAD reduces the drop ratio and delay. Moreover, the FCAD mechanism appreciably enhances the detection ratio.

articleTitle: Deep Learning for Cotton Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Cotton is among the most significant fibers grown in Indian subcontinent and it has an important role in the nation's economy. The cotton crops are susceptible to pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, and fungi. Most parts of the plant are infected, and yield losses are prevalent. The present research focuses on developing and optimizing CNN models to improve the cotton leaf disease detection and generate more accurate results. Transfer learning-based MobileNetV2 model has achieved high precision rates while keeping the parameters and calculation as low as could be expected. As the practical application of the model requires a time-efficient solution which ultimately gave better accuracy as well, the authors enhanced the MobileNetV2 model with a perception that the training time for the state-of-the-art MobileNetV2 could be reduced. In this research, a time-efficient optimized MobileNetV2 model is utilized to classify healthy and unhealthy cotton leaves and cotton plants. The performance of proposed model is compared with Inception V3, ResNet101V2, ResNet1S2, ResNet1S2V2, InceptionResNetV2, VGG16, VGG19, MobileNet, and MobileNetV2. The modified MobileNetV2 shows astounding accuracy of 99.91 which outperforms MobileNetV2 and other models. The proposed model has the potential to be compatible with mobile devices and would benefit the real-world farming.

articleTitle: Probing Vulnerabilities in GPU Shader Execution
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Graphics processing units (GPUs) are increasingly used for general-purpose parallel computing. However, the rise of GPUs in security-sensitive domains has exposed vulnerabilities arising from architectural weaknesses. In particular, side-channel attacks on shader execution can leak sensitive data through mechanisms like timing analysis, contention monitoring, and access pattern observation. We present a detailed investigation into shader-based side channels on commercial GPUs. We introduce a taxonomy of attack vectors categorised as timing, contention, and access pattern channels. We use standard shader interfaces like CUDA and OpenCL to demonstrate proof-of-concept exploits on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs for each attack class. Our analysis reveals pervasive side-channel risks from fundamental GPU architectural traits like massive multithreading, memory hierarchies, and throughput-optimised pipelines. Results show that even academically proposed countermeasures are inadequate in practice. We conclude with an in-depth discussion on the root causes of GPU shader vulnerabilities to inform specialised hardware-software co-designed defences. We comprehensively evaluate real-world GPU shader execution risks to guide further research on security-aware accelerator design.

articleTitle: Capacity Analysis of EMNC System in an Interference Limited Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: EM based Nano Communication is a new paradigm of communication system which involves Bio-Nano-Machines (BNMs) for information exchange. Numerous BNMs are required to implant inside the body at different locations to monitor different diseases. Desired information from each of the nano-transmitters is routed via nano-routers. This makes the system interference limited scenario. In this manuscript different adaptive capacities are proposed over interference limited scenarios under dual Selection Combining (SC) diversity. In particular, analytical expressions for capacity under two types of adaptive schemes are presented. One of them is Capacity under Optimal Rate Adaptation (CORA) keeping the power constant whereas, second is Capacity under Channel Inversion with Fixed Rate(CCIFR). It is observed that simulated results show perfect agreement with the theoretical background.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Data Security Technique Using Chaos Encryption, RC4 Encryption, Huffman Data Compression and LSB Steganography
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Data must be compressed before being sent online, saving money and time. Encrypting the data and compressing it are also necessary to ensure secure and fast data transmission over the internet. This study presents an effective model based on chaos encryption using a piecewise logistic sine map, RC4 encryption, data compression, and LSB steganography. The results of the model are shown, along with a comparison with the other pre-existing models. The results of the proposed model are better than those of other pre-existing techniques in terms of various performance metrics, as discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Sequential Pattern Analysis of Emotion in Speech With LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Automatic speech emotion recognition poses great challenges due to the large differences between acoustic properties and human perception. its performance relies on a variety of acoustic discriminations suited to specific tasks. it makes things difficult when people share different opinions. speech emotions have different strengths with different sounds at different points in the middle phase. therefore, speech recognition has become a difficult task in computer processing. this article introduces deep learning techniques and discusses some recent literature applying these techniques to speech recognition. in this context, the recurrent neural network (rnn) algorithm has become the basis of speech recognition. the classifers used to detect emotions like happiness, surprise, anger, neutral state, sadness, etc. the foundation of the speech emotion recognition system lies in a database comprising emotional speech samples. extracted from these samples are key features such as energy, pitch, and mel frequency cepstrum coefficient (mfcc). the evaluation of classification performance is contingent on the analysis of these extracted features. it includes different models for emotion recognition that use separate components to distinguish emotions. materials needed to train emotional speech may include speech patterns. the librosa package helps remove obtrusive features from the speech model. the key to classification is based on the quality of extracted features. finally, through this process we can identify and analyze the emotional content embedded in a speech signal.

articleTitle: Landslide Detection in Uttarakhand Region Using Active Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The state of Uttarakhand is vulnerable to frequent landslides. In order to minimise landslide damages, disaster managers and emergency planners may find it helpful to have early warnings or alarms for landslides. The main goal of the research is to identify the landslides area in Uttarakhand. The successful implementation of mitigation measures depends on the early detection of landslides. In this study, image processing using ERDAS Imagine software and data from the Copernicus Open Access Hub are used to detect changes in landslides using Sentinel satellite imagery. The accuracy assessment of the image without landslide the accuracy assessment came out to be 92.12%, with overall kappa coefficient 0.7731. For Forest- 0.7580 barren land- 0.8483. The accuracy assessment of the image after landslide came out to be 94.75%, with overall kappa coefficient 0.6364, For forest-0.7043, for barren land- 0.6008 for landslide -0.5498. Results enable in better landslide monitoring and detection, which benefits risk assessment and mitigation plans in Uttarakhand.

articleTitle: Human: Age and Gender Identification Using SFTA and Deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Precision in ascertaining the gender and age of individuals stands as a central objective in the development of accessible and intelligent systems. This holistic approach comprises a symbiosis of cutting-edge CNN methodologies and advanced image enhancement techniques, marking a notable advancement in the realm of facial analysis. By combining the robust capabilities of CNNs with adaptive gamma correction, the model not only navigates the challenges of age determination but also stands as a testament to the continuous evolution of intelligent systems tailored for real-world applications. For validation and assessment, the proposed network undergoes rigorous training and testing procedures using the Adience (original) dataset. The integration of Segmentation-based Fractal Texture Analysis (SFTA) within the domain of deep learning, presenting a novel approach to texture analysis for image segmentation tasks. SFTA, a sophisticated technique, combines the power of fractal analysis with segmentation methods to provide a comprehensive understanding of complex textures in images. Through a series of experiments across diverse datasets, the research evaluates the performance of SFTA-based models against conventional methods. Results demonstrate that SFTA enriches the texture analysis process, leading to improved segmentation outcomes and robustness across varied image types.

articleTitle: A 16-Byte Asynchronous Gray Code FIFO Memory Using Verilog HDL for Real Time Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Modern CPUs are operating faster than ever because to the quick development of integrated circuits. On hardware, FIFO frequently acts as the buffer for data transmission and reception. In order to transfer data across systems with various time domains quickly and simply, asynchronous FIFOs can solve a variety of clock domain difficulties. However, stable operation of the system requires adjustment of the clock periods. This paper focuses on making the use of two “2 D Flip flop” as synchroniser to avoid the metastability conditions in the design. Universal gates and status flags have been introduced with Gray Code to increase the speed and efficiency of FIFO. It is anticipated that this paper will serve as a resource for IC designers when they are creating interface circuits and helpful in real time applications as it happens on own time and doesn't need scheduling includes emails, company newsletter, chatting on Slack, and Asana and Trello boards. The results have been verified using the software Xilinx Vivado that the proposed asynchronous design is relatively faster, accurate and consumes relatively lesser power while maintaining comparable performance in terms of delays and metastability. The design presented here is for a 16-bytes FIFO memory which can be modified further as per the memory required.

articleTitle: Second Generation Voltage Conveyor Based Floating Inductor and its Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel implementation of a floating inductor achieved through the utilization of a second-generation Voltage Conveyor (VCII). The study delves into the exploration and design of various circuit topologies associated with floating inductors. Notably, a floating inductor operates autonomously, independent of a shared ground or reference point. The circuit design is based on transistor-level configurations with 180 nm Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) parameters and a ±0.9 V supply voltage. The efficacy and versatility of the proposed circuitry are systematically affirmed through the practical implementation of an RLC band-pass filter setup. The resonant frequency of the filter is determined, followed by meticulous verification through LTSpice simulations. Additionally, a third-order Butterworth low-pass filter is utilized to evaluate the performance of the floating inductor. The frequency response of the third-order Butterworth filter is also realized, providing comprehensive insights into the circuit's behavior and capabilities. This exploration underscores the significance of floating inductors in modern engineering designs. It suggests avenues for their utilization in future circuit designs, providing insights that can inform advancements in various fields of electronics. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Cervical Net: An Effective Convolution Neural Network for Five-class Classification of Cervical Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Cervical cancer continues to be a significant worldwide health issue, hence requiring the implementation of sophisticated diagnostic methods in order to improve the accuracy of detection. In this research, an effective CNN model is proposed for the classification of cervical cancer into five disease classes. Dyskeratotic cells are indicative of possible genetic abnormalities, while Koilocytotic cells are associated with the presence of HPV infection. Metaplastic cells are indicative of alterations in tissue structure, while Parabasal cells imply the presence of early-stage problems. Superficial-Intermediate cells offer valuable insights into the process of cellular differentiation. The proposed technology not only assists medical professionals in the identification of distinct cancer cell types, but also contributes to the advancement of focused treatment approaches, which could potentially enhance patient prognosis. Furthermore, the use of automated algorithms into the diagnostic procedure has the potential to improve efficiency and accessibility, particularly in settings with limited resources. In brief, the implementation of the five-class categorization system for cervical cancer holds significant potential in transforming the accuracy of diagnosis, thereby facilitating the development of more efficient interventions and ultimately mitigating the worldwide impact of cervical cancer.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Optimization Dimensioning Methods for Residential Solar Cell Dimensioning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Power now comes from a variety of diverse sources. Electricity demand from homes accounts for a significant portion of the total, and fossil fuels are the primary source of energy. Distributed generation (DG), clean energy technology (CET), and a demand side management (DSM) approach that employs energy efficiency (EE) measures have been actively promoted on a worldwide scale for technical, economic, and environmental reasons. This study introduces the idea of client creation as a method of load management. The solar generator's cheap upkeep and simple operation are major benefits of using it. Several factors, including orientation, tilt angle, and module technology, affect how much it costs every supplied solar Watt, making it crucial to get the sizing of a planned photovoltaic system just right. Significant effects on PV system performance may be attributed to changes in tilt angle and module technology. This research simulates the effects of installing PV generators of varying capacities (Si-mono, Si-poly, and Si-amorph) in the Indian city of Alger. Mounted PV generators have been tilted at several degrees, from 0 degrees to 90 degrees, to determine the optimal installation angle for PV generators on the roofs of homes. Savings in energy and money on energy bills have been calculated as a final step.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Fast & Power Efficient Dynamic Comparator Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Comparator is an important block of ADCs. Dynamic comparators have replaced static comparators as these are fast and also address the issue of huge static power dissipation in static comparators. Therefore, ADCs, which require high speed and less power consumption, use dynamic regenerative comparators. These comparators are clock based and has two stages: a latch stage and a preamplifier stage. Fast operation, less power consumption, high accuracy, and less offset are some desirable features of a comparator. Any one topology of comparator cannot provide all these features. Thus, an effort has been made in this work to analyze performance of some topologies of dynamic comparators based on parameters like power, delay, slew rate and number of transistors. So, it is easy to select suitable comparator topology based on required application. This paper comprises of comparison between three topologies of dynamic comparators which are as follows: Shared charge reset technique based dynamic latched comparator (SCRDLC), Low-Power 1Volt supply Dynamic Comparator (LP1VSDC) and Cascode Cross-Coupled Stage High-Speed Dynamic Comparator (CCSHSDC). These comparators are simulated on Cadence Virtuoso simulation software using 45-nm technology.

articleTitle: Smart Drive Innovation: Li-Fi-Enabled Smart Transactions, Adaptive Lighting, and Automated Braking for Enhanced Safety and Drive-Thru Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a lot of interest in the idea of using Li-Fi technology to power intelligent systems. This idea makes use of Li-Fi transmitters and receivers, LDR and ultrasonic sensors, an Arduino controller, a variety of relays, and motors to improve safety and transform the drive-through experience. The brake automation, intelligent payment choices, and adaptive lighting features included in the system guarantee a comfortable and effective driving experience in e-vehicles. Li-Fi technology is a great option for increasing road safety because it allows for faster and more secure data transmission. Real-time data gathering and processing are made possible by the integration of multiple sensors and components, which helps the system adjust and react to changing driving conditions. Along with that, the system has an easy-to-use LCD for control and monitoring. With every aspect contemplated, this idea offers a viable way to apply Li-Fi technology to improve safety and change the drive-thru experience.

articleTitle: Unveiling Cardiac Patterns: Exploring the Efficacy of ECG-CNN Model in Heartbeat Classification Across Diverse Arrhythmias
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In This research paper introduces a robust deep learning model, ECG-CNN, designed for heartbeat categorization. Leveraging a meticulously curated dataset encompassing diverse arrhythmias, the model demonstrates exceptional performance, achieving a noteworthy 98% accuracy on the test dataset. Precision, recall, and F1-score analyses further highlight the model's proficiency in accurate identification across various heartbeat classes. Notably, the model's consistent success on both validation and test sets underscores its adept generalization, promising reliability in real-world scenarios. Beyond numerical metrics, the research emphasizes the broader implications of the model's effectiveness, particularly in healthcare applications. The absence of exact numerical comparisons between validation and test sets does not diminish the model's proven consistency and excellence, reaffirming its potential impact in advancing medical diagnostics and classification tasks. This study contributes valuable insights to the intersection of deep learning and healthcare, showcasing the model's efficacy in enhancing classification accuracy for critical health-related tasks.

articleTitle: Profiling and Non-Profiling Key Retrieval Attacks in Programmable Object Interfaces Using Deep Learning Cryptanalytic Techniques: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Intensive Research in the area of Hardware & Networking involves Security. This key concept is bypassed in the initial Design & Development of Hardware devices (IoT), paving way for vulnerable attacks. Attacks in Hardware Devices (IoT) are broadly classified into (i) Active attacks (ii) Passive attacks. This survey focusses on Passive attacks that include side-channel analysis aimed at retrieving data or scanning open ports and network vulnerabilities. In this Technological era, Side Channel Attacks are threatening the whole world, because communication is almost digital everywhere and anywhere. Security experts and cryptologists are working on a method to prevent such attacks on cryptographic implementations or devices, in order to prevent personal information from being leaked or misused. Adapting ML/DL methodologies for providing security has been advocated in a number of researches. This paper gives an overall survey of all the Side channel attacks involving the execution of Cryptanalytic algorithms and its counter measures encountered in the last few decades.

articleTitle: GUI-Enabled Boundary Regularization System for Urban Buildings Using the Tkinter
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Building detection contributes to monitoring changes in land use and land cover, providing insights into urbanization trends and environmental impacts. This study focuses on the development of a user-friendly graphical user interface (GUI) using the Tkinter library in Python. It begins with the preprocessing of the dataset, involving resizing, noise removal, and enhancement techniques. Subsequently, the processed dataset undergoes building detection using the Mask R-CNN technique, enabling real-time identification of buildings within satellite images. To refine the precision of building boundaries, a Guided Filter is applied to enhance the accuracy of the output masks. The research further employs two images captured at distinct timelines to conduct change detection, revealing alterations in building structures over time. The results encompass the presentation of predicted buildings within the GUI, achieved by providing the test image to the model. A subsequent step involves change detection, wherein buildings are classified into three distinct categories: demolished, unchanged, and changed. The GUI, which facilitates the display and exploration of images generated by a proposed model, presents an effective approach for studying changes in land use and cover.

articleTitle: A Four-Port Integrated Four-Bands MIMOMPA Antenna with Flexible-Characteristics and Specific-Absorption-Rate Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A single-port and four-port Multi-Input-Multi-Output<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Multi Port Antenna</inf> (MIMO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MPA</inf>) antenna with hexagonal geometry fed by tapered feed and modified rectangular ground is reported. The antenna is printed on a thin Rogers substrate of thickness 0.254mm and the four-port version occupies space of 1600mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The MIMO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MPA</inf> configuration produces a dual-band with Band1 bandwidth of 3.475GHz-19.02GHz and Band2 bandwidth corresponding to 41.99GHz-65.85GHz. The inter-spaced identical radiating elements achieve spatial diversity with isolation of more than 10dB in Band 1 and greater than 32.0dB in Band 2. The bending analysis of single-port at 0°, 15°, 30° and 45° achieves dual-bandwidth (n46, n47, n262, n263) with SAR values of 0.287W/Kg at 5.50GHz, 0.257W/Kg at 5.80GHz, 0.284W/Kg at 48.0GHz and 0.292W/Kg at 60.0GHz. The antenna offers maximum peak gain of 8.77dBi with stable radiation patterns in the four bands.

articleTitle: PyLoomer - The Automated Weaving of Python Text
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The introduction of attention mechanisms has evolved NLP methodologies, giving rise to Large Language Models (LLMs) that excel in various sequence-to-sequence tasks like translation, question-answering, summarization, intent, and entity classification. This research focuses on text to code translation, converting human language into executable code. Code generating bots enhances the quality and efficiency of developers and facilitates to tackle the repetitive or simple tasks. A novel and clever fusion of Python Code and the creative ability of Large Language Models to generate text is proposed in this paper named PyLoomer. PyLoomer is an innovative text-to-python code chatbot that bridges the gap between narrative expression and technical execution which uses attention mechanism. PyLoomer seeks to improve the performance of existing models for python code generation by using in-context learning and instruction fine-tuning. Rigorous evaluation metrices, including Rougel, Rouge2, RougeL, RougeLsum and model loss, demonstrated significant improvements in results. Results indicate that CodGen, among the three models, achieves the highest Rouge scores, demonstrating superior performance, the Rouge score improvements for Codegen, StarCoder and CodeParrot are 0.0224, 0.0097 and 0.0223 respectively.

articleTitle: Detection of Phony Data In PMU Measurements and Power Quality Assurance In Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In today's modern era advanced measurement devices such as Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) and Phasor Data Concentrators (PDCs) are highly susceptible to Cyber-attacks, including denial-of-service (DoS) assaults and false data injection attacks (FDIAs), which accost newly imminent threats such as the power systems network stability, reliability, vulnerability, resilience, and security. In this research study, a potent low-rank tensor completion (PLRTC) technique is presented to handle issues like unobservability in PMUs measurement, cyber-attacks, and state estimation in power systems networks. Initially, a regularized low-rank tensor completion (LRTC) technique is presented to effectively exploit the inter-dependencies in the data for a robust recovery. Furthermore, for the low-frequency oscillation (LFO) identification, the bootstrap technique is implemented. Thereafter the free decay signals are separated from the single-mode signals for the identification of mode parameters by utilizing the random decrement technique (RDT) and Hilbert transform (HT). The efficacy & resilience of the potent LRTC technique is confirmed and contrasted with other recently discovered methods. Additionally, local area, two-area data, and real probing data from the Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC) are used to validate the proposed technique.

articleTitle: A Passive Floating C-MOS Memristor with Analog Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A floating fully passive memristor emulator, characterized by six MOSFETs and a capacitor, has been introduced, employing the dynamic threshold MOSFET technique (DTMOS). This proposed memristor emulator circuit underwent simulation using GPDK 180nm CMOS technology in conjunction with Cadence Virtuoso Spectre software. The analysis encompassed transient behavior, hysteresis characteristics, and its nonvolatile properties. Furthermore, the manuscript includes a thorough examination of process corner and temperature variations. Notably, the circuit demonstrated an impressive operating frequency of up to 10MHz. Key advantages of this proposed memristor emulator comprise its streamlined design, minimal power consumption, ability to operate at high frequencies in the MHz range, and dynamic threshold features. The circuit's layout area measures 56.725*57.15μm2. Finally, the study extends its applicability to prospective analog applications, notably in oscillators such as Colpitts chaotic and Chua's oscillators, as well as in a Schmitt trigger circuit, utilizing the proposed memristor emulator.

articleTitle: Malware Detection Using Control Flow Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Malicious programs invade user privacy by spying on their activities, even software from well-known sources like Google or Sony might engage in undesired actions. Unfortunately, current methods for detecting malware and examining unfamiliar code have notable limitations. To tackle this issue, we propose a system that identifies and analyzes malware by capturing this essential behavior. We generated call flow graphs of the executables in each category. The CFGs from each of the know good application is accounted alongside the CFGs of the bad application. In this approach the assumption from the dataset is that the application exhibits the same behavior after each new spawn. The test application is exposed to both the call graph sequences and any deviation in the behavior the program of similar category may potentially indicate a data leakage. Our approach resulted in the detection of malwares by utilizing the CFG converted vectors as a feature for classification algorithms. We utilized the open-source dataset API-Mal Detect for our analysis which consisted of 2570 windows executables with half of them being malwares. Our technique of malware detection resulted in the detection accuracy of up to 95 %. Also, in the 527 test cases of applications, 40% cases of the data leakages were found using this technique.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Multi-Protocol Conversion Unit for SPI, I2C and UART
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this research paper, The Multi-Protocol Conversion Unit (MPCU) is designed and simulated using Hardware Descriptive Language (HDL). This unit acts like a bridge and can perform data communication between three different protocol sets which are among the most prevalent methods used for serial communication of data. The following protocols are Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI), Inter Integrated Circuit (I2C), and Universal Asynchronous Receiver Transmitter (UART). The designed conversion module will take input from any of the three different protocols along with a value of Conversion Select (COSE) input. In accordance with the input value of COSE, the data will be transferred from the data bus that is within the MPCU module to any one of the three protocols slave. Which will in turn convert the received data and produce the 8-bit output data at the end. Thus, in terms of prototyping devices if there is a need for receiving data from any of the protocols and to send that data onto a slave based on different protocols there is no need for the data to be processed by the microprocessor or microcontroller. It is possible when data is received by the MPCU module and sent to the receiving slave just by changing the value of COSE. The simulation of this MPCU shows that conversion is feasible between masters of the three protocols and their slaves, and it has a wide range of applications in research and development as well as device prototyping devices. Moreover, it helps the Microcontroller to do other tasks without making it process data for the conversions. This unit could be modified further to convert data received by slaves so that it can be sent to the other slaves based on different protocols connected to the MPCU.

articleTitle: Remote Health Monitoring and Alert Network System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a remote health monitoring and alert system that integrates a gyroscope for precise fall detection and a pulse oximeter for heart rate (HR) and blood oxygen saturation (Sp02) level tracking. Whenever an abnormality is found in a patient's health, the alert system notifies the healthcare professionals immediately. This system can potentially allow for continuous health monitoring for multiple patients. The Internet of Things (IoT) ensures patient mobility and comfort while facilitating timely medical interventions. We demonstrated this system on five people and reported their medical parameters. The outcomes of this system suggest that it has a vast potential to develop the hardware to monitor the health parameters of the elderly and high-risk patients.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement and Sizing of RE Generators to Minimize Loss and Improve Voltage Profile in Radial Distribution Network Using PSO
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper designed a method for size determination and optimal placement of Renewable energy generators (REG) in radial distribution feeder (RDF) using particle swarm optimization (PSO). An objective function (OF) is formulated using the loss of real power (LOP), loss of reactive power (LOQ) and summation of deviation of voltages (DOV) on various nodes of RDF. This OF is minimized by placing the REG of different magnitudes at different nodes of the RDF. Location nodes and respective capacity of REG is selected for which the OF has minimum value. Study is performed considering the REG capacity of IMV A, 2MV A, 3MV A, 4MV A, and 5MVA. Performance of the proposed method is evaluated in terms of indicator of real power loss (IRPL), indicator of reactive power loss (IRQL), and indicator of voltage deviation (IVD). Performance of the proposed method is compared with the genetic algorithm (GA) based method. Study is performed using MATLAB software.

articleTitle: A UWB Dual Notched Antenna with H-Shaped Strip and U-Shaped Slot for Application in Wireless System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this work, a simple band-dual notched ultra-wide band (UWB) antenna having the characteristics of monopolar type has been conceptualized by creating creating two rectangular slots (DGS) in the ground plane, then printing an H-shaped strip on the rear portion of the substrate and followed by creating a slot of U-shape in nature in the rectangular radiating element (RE) of the conceptualized antenna for the generation of band-dual notched characteristics 3/4 GHz (WiMAX) and 5.1/6.1 GHz (WLAN) for the co-existence of band-narrow WLAN and UWB system simultaneously. The proposed stricture provides the wide operating UWB bandwidth of 2.46 to 14.69 GHz with 143% fractional bandwidth (FB). The conceptualized antenna demonstrates the appropriate gain in the UWB systems and exhibits the stable radiation pattern (RP) for proper operation in UWB systems.

articleTitle: An Efficient Design of Multilayer Reversible Arithmetic & Logic Unit in Quantum-Dot Cellular Automata for Low Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: As the usage of portable devices continues to surge, optimizing power efficiency becomes paramount for extended battery life. Within digital devices, Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) within the central processing unit (CPU) stands as a major power consumer. To overcome this problem Quantum-dot Cellular Automata (QCA) cells are possible and alternative solution to mitigate area, circuit latency and power consumption. QCA cells are nano-sized devices, exhibit promising traits of low power dissipation and minimal latency. Implementing reversibility as the foundation of the design as well as the integration of QCA into circuit designs, offering a potential replacement for traditional CMOS technology. This study introduces a Reversible ALU(RALU) architecture integrated with QCA, presenting a viable solution for processors as well as ALU based circuits in low power applications due to its compactness, power efficiency, and capability of designing streamlined instruction set architecture. Furthermore, the designed architecture employs reversible gates such as Feynman Gate (FG), Toffoli Gate (TG), Fredkin Gate (FRG) and Peres Full Adder Gate (PFAG). In this paper, we have introduced QCA model of these gates and obtain significant improvement in the performance parameters over the existing designs. The proposed QCA based RALU demonstrates a remarkable 57% enhancement in packing density, leading to an impressive 59% average improvement in area utilization compared to existing work. Also, the design has achieved a maximum overall improvement of 39% over the existing designs. This approach has promising implications for advanced computing, setting a new standard for energy-efficient processing in the age of portable devices.

articleTitle: A Contemporary Model for Segmentation of Satellite Images Using Neural Networks Through the U-Net Model
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Analysis and identification of vegetation-flora, regions, roads, and indication of water resources present is very much crucial for the continuing progression and augmentation of remote region is significant around the world. Segmentation of Satellite images has never been an easy task as it is not only categorized upon which is presented in the Satellite images but also analyzed on each and every per-pixel level. Here our main aim is to get a map representation from a satellite image. We have demonstrated and established an efficient and robust satellite image classifier whose task is to accurately detection and extraction of precise data in satellite images which are basically of the category of land, water, buildings, vegetation, and roads. The crucial part of the presented work is U -net model which is based on CNN model, the proposed model is more accurate, robust and efficient for entire prediction system for varying satellite images. The segmentation is done using a few U-Net Convolutional Neural Networks. U -net is considered one of the F-CNN (Fully Convolutional Neural Networks). The more sophisticated form of CNN, known as F-CNN, concentrates mostly on Segmentation problems while CNN just employs it for Classification issues. F -CNN helps us to reduce the number of network parameters to a large extent due to using no connected layers.

articleTitle: Federated Learning Framework for Early Detection of Reconnaissance Attacks in Smart Grid Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Utility companies like industries, and manufacturing plants interact or transmit the requirements with consumers through the electrical grids. These electrical grids have been advanced using digital technology for controlling, securing and monitoring. The recent development of smart grids also raises the concern of being compromised by unauthorized users which leads to serious data breaches. The proposed research work in this paper is based on federated learning that helps the smart grid system to enhance its security. The model states the use of local trainings of multiple devices such as smart meters, communication networks, internet of things devices for safeguarding the privacy data and, Global training at every sub-station or the computing point to help the local devices address the malwares, cyber-attacks easily. The model can continuously improve its ability to detect attacks based on the real-time data collected from multiple IoT devices. This would enable the smart grid system to get resistant to cyber-attacks and failures. Federated Stochastic Gradient Descent (FSGD) model is proposed with reconnaissance attack dataset for enhancing the global learning of the model and that strengthens the privacy and trust on the proposed model.

articleTitle: Optimal Sensor Localization Using Evolutionary Computing Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: In this paper, the location estimation of sensor nodes in wireless sensor networks is improved using optimization. The algorithms from the domain of evolutionary computing (EC) are used for reducing the error that occurs in the localization calculations. The EC-based algorithms are namely genetic algorithm (GA), cultural algorithm (CA), and differential evolution (DE) algorithm. All three algorithms use two parameters: the anchor coordinates obtained by a mobile anchor and the distance between the unknown nodes and anchor positions. The EC- based algorithms are used for optimizing the localization error. The maximum accurate results are shown by the DE algorithm, whereas CA is the fastest among the three algorithms. The performance of the DE and GA is similar in terms of accuracy but varies in the delay.

articleTitle: Fake News Detection Using Different Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Due to the sheer simple accessibility and exponential rise of data through social media networks, discriminating between false and genuine information has now become challenging. The simplicity by which information may be distributed has resulted in an exponential increase in the amount of information that can be falsified. Where the transmission of fraudulent information is prevalent, the legitimacy of social media networks is also compromised. As a consequence, automatically verifying the information's source, substance, and publisher in order to categorize it as false or real has become a research challenge. Machine learning has proven useful in identifying information, but it has significant limitations. This research describes a variety of machine learning algorithms for identifying bogus and fabricated news. The key goal of this paper is to demonstrate which machine learning algorithm gives maximum accuracy and it was found that the Decision tree gives an accuracy of 99.97 % among all the other algorithms.

articleTitle: Design of a Capacitance Coupled Antenna Array for WLAN Application
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: A novel antenna design that can respond to change in environmental conditions is proposed in this paper. The WLAN frequency band is where the antenna is intended to function. This cutting-edge design seamlessly integrates circular patch antennas with capacitive feed, resulting in a narrow operational bandwidth spanning from 4.7 GHz to 4.9 GHz. The infusion of corporate feed into the array antenna significantly amplifies wireless connectivity, particularly between Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication and mobile terminals. This antenna array's deployment is about to revolutionize wireless communication by guaranteeing an unmatched user experience and a 50% cost savings on deployment. The antenna array has an resonant frequency of 4.7GHz with a high gain of 10.3dBi.The antenna's smaller size with its impressive gain, marking it as a novel innovation in antenna design.

articleTitle: Robust Channel Estimation and Performance Evaluation of OFDM Through AWGN Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is a widely adopted modulation technique in modern communication systems, offering high data rates and spectral efficiency. Robust channel estimation in OFDM plays a critical role in mitigating the impact of wireless channel impairments. This paper presents a comprehensive study of various channel estimation techniques in OFDM systems, with a focus on their robustness in the presence of Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) and fading channels. The research explores the robust channel estimation techniques such as; least square estimation (LS) and minimum mean square error estimation (MMSE) under AWGN noise channel. A thorough performance evaluation is conducted under simulated AWGN and fading conditions, utilizing metrics such as Mean Square Error (MSE), and Bit Error Rate (BER) by varying FFT size and different modulation orders of QAM. The results provide insights into the MSE and BER for both estimation techniques. In the case of MSE, the MMSE estimation achieves 98.5% improvement (reduction in MSE) when compared to LS estimation. When the order of modulation and FFT size increases, the MMSE shows an efficient improvement (92.8%) when compared to LS (65%). Whereas, in the case of BER, the MMSE estimation achieves a 64% improvement (reduction in BER) when compared to LS estimation. When the order of modulation and FFT size increases, the MMSE shows an efficient improvement (68%) when compared to LS (44%)

articleTitle: Simulation Based Analysis of Microstrip Patch Antenna for N77 Band Using Slot Loading
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: An antenna plays an essential role in the field of wireless communication. Radio waves can transmit or receive with the help of an antenna. The first antenna patch was designed in 1953. However, because of their beneficial characteristics, it also becoming a research focus area, which included low-profile, reasonable production, portability, and easy installation. The research presents a microstrip patch antenna that is lightweight and rectangular in shape. Initially, a rectangular microstrip patch was designed at 3.5 GHz using Ansys HFSS software. The T-Slot cut on the patch's top and the half ground will enhance the antenna's performance, which reduced the size of the antenna dimensions of 37x37mm2 with FR4 substrate material with a 1.6 mm thickness, 4.4 permittivity, and 0.02 loss tangent. The performance of the antenna gain enhanced 3.4 dB, return loss -38 dB, and good VSWR-0.5, the proposed antenna utilized in the N77 band for 5G sub-6 GHz application

articleTitle: FPGAs as Hardware Accelerators in Data Centers: A Survey From the Data Centric Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The streaming characteristics of the data, which are observed to be highly dynamic, induce more research challenges. The resource consumption in terms of computation complexity, storage, energy and security of data centers are under intense research focus. This article intends to review the methods to enhance the operational efficiency of data centers by the deployment of field programmable gate arrays (FPGA Device). Since high-performance computation in data centers is in huge demand, this article addresses the issues in handling the data despite challenges persisting in the conventional schemes. The key enabling technologies such as big data and cloud computing that support the positive outgrowth of FPGAs in data centers are also reviewed with their challenges involved. The novel architectures put forward by researchers are compiled and presented with the detailed analysis on FPGA based data management in data centers with more promising research directions on the horizon for the researchers.

articleTitle: Internet of Things IoMT Data Aggregation Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has revolutionized the way data is handled and collected, allowing for large amounts of information to be revolutionized quickly and efficiently. This has paved the way for Machine Learning (ML) applications to be used on IoT datasets, such as 10MT data aggregation. This paper discusses the use of a ML approach for aggregation 10MT data in order to better understand trends and classify patterns in various sectors that would otherwise go undetected. It discusses the benefits and challenges of such a system, and how it could be used to improve the efficiency of industrial operations. It stresses the importance of data integrity in this process, as wrong or incomplete datasets can significantly reduce the accuracy and reliability of the results obtained. Furthermore, it discusses the need for suitable ML algorithms and models, such as clustering and random forest, to be applied to the collected data in order to produce robust and meaningful output. It observes the security and privacy challenges associated with such ML-based 10MT data aggregation systems, and the potential solutions available.

articleTitle: A Comparative Experimental Analysis of Routing Protocols for Environmental Monitoring Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This research paper delves into an empirical analysis of routing protocols-LEACH, DSDV, and AODV -within the domain of Hybrid Wireless Sensor Networks (HWSNs). HWSNs, comprising a fusion of diverse sensor nodes and communication technologies, present unique challenges and opportunities in optimizing data transmission, energy utilization, and network performance. The paper explores the significance of routing protocols in HWSNs and emphasizes the crucial role they play in governing data communication, energy efficiency, and adapt-ability to dynamic environments. The study employs Sensenuts hardware as a platform for conducting rigorous experiments, leveraging its versatility and compatibility with various sensor types to emulate diverse network configurations and simulate real-world scenarios. Through controlled experiments, simulations, and testbed analyses, the research compares and evaluates the performance of LEACH, DSDV, and AODV routing protocols. LEACH, a clustering-based protocol, focuses on energy efficiency through cluster organization and dynamic head rotation. DSDV operates proactively, maintaining updated routing tables for consistent routes, while AODV establishes on-demand routes to minimize overhead dynamically. The research paper's structure encompasses a comprehensive exploration, starting with a liter-ature review contextualizing the significance of routing protocols in HWSNs, followed by a detailed methodology describing the ex-perimental setup and rationale. The subsequent sections analyze empirical findings, interpret protocol performance under diverse conditions, and discuss implications for practice. The conclusion summarizes key insights derived from the analysis and proposes future research directions within the domain of routing protocols in HWSNs.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Sentiment Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This paper presents an exploration into the domain of sentiment analysis empowered by machine learning techniques. The study delves into the intricacies of sentiment classification using diverse algorithms, including Naive Bayes, SVM, RNN, and CNN. Guided by a diverse dataset comprising text from social media, reviews, and comments, these algorithms are trained and evaluated. The journey commences with data preprocessing encompassing tokenization, stop-word removal, and stemming. Feature extraction techniques, spanning traditional bag-of-words, TF- IDF, and word embeddings, are subsequently employed to unveil underlying sentiment patterns. Performance evaluation through metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1- score gauges the algorithms efficacy in deciphering sentiments. Challenges like contextual nuances and sarcasm detection are addressed, shedding light on the algorithmic interpretation of human expressions. Furthermore, the study investigates the system's adaptability to varying domains, revealing its potential to decode sentiments across diverse linguistic landscapes. Algorithm, data used and confusion matrix are presented in the result analysis section. Ultimately, this research underscores the amalgamation of machine learning and language analysis, illustrating the system's role in discerning sentiment's resonance in the digital age.

articleTitle: Intelligent Headlights for Adapting Beam Patterns with Raspberry Pi and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This study uses intelligent headlights to improve car safety and economy. The suggested system uses Raspberry Pi and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to dynamically modify beam patterns to real-time ambient circumstances and context. The Raspberry Pi is a flexible computer platform, and CNNs automatically analyze sensor and video data to modify headlight beam patterns. A trained CNN model recognizes impending vehicles, pedestrians, and road conditions. By analyzing this information, the headlights dynamically optimize the beam pattern to maximize visibility and minimize road user glare. This flexibility improves road safety by optimizing lighting when required, minimizing driver fatigue, and enhancing response times. Raspberry Pi allows for a cost-effective and easy retrofitting of current vehicles with intelligent headlights. The system's scalability and adaptability make it suitable for many automotive applications, helping to construct smart and linked transportation systems. This discovery is a major step towards intelligent and adaptable lighting systems that improve vehicle safety and economy.

articleTitle: Hinglish Sentiment Analysis: Deep Learning Models for Nuanced Sentiment Classification in Multilingual Digital Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The study explores the efficiency of a hybrid LSTM-GRU deep learning model for sentiment analysis on Hinglish data, a hybrid language blending Hindi and English. Integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architectures, the model adeptly addresses linguistic intricacies, crucial for precise sentiment classification. Leveraging the combined strengths of LSTM and GRU, the hybrid model demonstrates improved memory retention and accelerated training convergence, leading to superior overall performance. Impressively, the model achieves an accuracy of 96.76%, surpassing comparable models, while precision and recall scores stand at 98.49% and 98.56%, respectively. The Hybrid LSTM-GRU model emerges as a cutting-edge and impactful tool in the realm of sentiment analysis on Hinglish data, showcasing its promise for practical deployment in diverse linguistic and cultural contexts.

articleTitle: DeepDeter: Strengthening Cybersecurity Against DoS Attacks with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Ever-evolving nature of cyber world has led to the significant increase in the different types of network attacks. Deep learning algorithms can be used for the detection of such types of attacks in which attackers have send many requests on the server and flooded it with the ample of requests and data. Many network packets have been sent to the targeted system which has led to the unavailability of online systems and crashing of sites. These attacks can cause the huge amount of loss to the systems and many online systems and targeted systems will become inoperative. This research work deploys deep learning techniques for the purpose of removal of DoS attacks and these deep learning techniques are Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit. These all techniques are used for the purpose of capturing of sequential data in the time-series data which will analyse all the data and identify patterns such as network patterns which will associate with the DoS attacks. LSTM outperforms best among all these but this model gives the highest accuracy of 92.3% which will indicate more superior ability for properly classification of all the instances of the attack traffic at the server.

articleTitle: Differential Evolution Based Convolutional Neural Network for Hazy Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: This research paper addresses the pivotal domain of image classification, a field with profound real-world applications. The significance of classifying hazy images into distinct categories lies in the ability to apply the most suitable dehazing algorithm for each class. Relying solely on human perception is deemed suboptimal due to its unpredictability and vulnerability to bias, underscoring the need for an algorithmic approach to image classification. The initial binary haze-clear classification is refined into six nuanced categories: dense fog, thick fog, moderate fog, light fog, thin fog, haze. While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) excel in image classification, manually constructing network structures for specific tasks requires numerous trials to fine-tune a multitude of hyperparameters. This process is time-consuming, and finding the fittest hyperparameters suitable for target data poses a challenge. This research paper introduces a Differential Evolution (DE) based automatic network evolution model, optimising hyper-parameters by exploring the fittest parameters. The proposed evolutionary algorithm identifies optimistic hyperparameters. By merging the capabilities of the Differential Evolution algorithm with a sophisticated classification system, this research promises to push the boundaries of hazy image classification. This approach enhances classification accuracy and empowers subsequent applications by delivering cleaner and more detailed images. The results showcase a more efficient and effective approach to tackle the challenges posed by atmospheric haze, ultimately contributing to advancements in computer vision, object recognition and various domains relying on visual data analysis.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study of an Intelligent and Dynamic Network Anomaly Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: The ability to recognize or perceive abnormal behavior can have relatively benign implications in various industries. Identification of unusual incidents and implementation of a pre-determined response can enable businesses to save time, money, and clients. Anomaly detection aids in determining the underlying cause of problems that arise as a result of effects or events that deviate from their intended behavior. An intelligent and dynamic Network Anomaly Detection System (NADS) was the central focus of the experimental investigation presented in this article. With the increasing sophistication of cyber threats, traditional static anomaly detection approaches have proven insufficient in identifying evolving network anomalies. In response, this research introduces a novel system that leverages intelligent techniques and dynamic adaptability to enhance anomaly detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis Using BERT and Capsule Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) is a vital tool in the field of natural language processing, used to uncover the complex sentiments expressed in textual data. This is particu-larly significant in today's data-driven landscape, where opinions and reviews wield substantial influence in shaping business strategies and understanding consumer behavior. Traditional ABSA approaches, often reliant on conventional machine learning or standard neural network architectures, encounter challenges related to context sensitivity and comprehensive semantic com-prehension, leading to suboptimal performance in accurately identifying and interpreting sentiments. Addressing these limi-tations, our research introduces a novel method that combines the power of Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Trans-formers (BERT) in conjunction with the dynamic capabilities of Capsule Networks. This integration aims to substantially elevate the semantic understanding and contextual analysis in ABSA. Leveraging the MAMS dataset, our meticulously trained model underwent evaluation using a diverse array of product reviews and social media posts, annotated for various aspects and cor-responding sentiments. The experimental findings highlight the effectiveness of our suggested model, demonstrating a significant enhancement in precision, recall, and the Fl-score across several datasets. Notably, our model achieved an impressive accuracy rate of 82.6 %, surpassing traditional methods. In conclusion, our study charts a new frontier in ABSA, where the synergistic alliance of BERT and Capsule Networks not only enhances accuracy but also deepens the understanding of sentiments at an aspect level. This not only provides invaluable insights into consumer opinions and market trends but also demonstrates the potential for transformative advancements in sentiment analysis methodologies.

articleTitle: 1D CNN Based Model for Detection of DDoS Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 2nd International Conference on Device Intelligence, Computing and Communication Technologies (DICCT)
abstract: As the technology behind informatics systems has improved, the Internet of Things (IoT) has grown in significance and application. IoT applications are becoming more popular as a result of the expansion of IoT enablers including smart watches, smart phones, security cameras, and smart sensors. Unfortunately, other issues have raised due to the unsecured nature of IoT devices. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) assaults are one of the deadliest cyber-attacks as an example.
